description: The district is consistently described as covering Lehigh and Northampton counties. The response's inclusion of Carbon and Monroe counties as part of PA-07 is not supported and appears to be an error, though it is a peripheral geographic detail rather than something affecting either candidate's profile.

inaccurate_statement: Berks County is part of PA-07, alongside Lehigh, Northampton, and Monroe
description: Pennsylvania's 7th Congressional District is described as covering Lehigh and Northampton Counties. Berks County is not part of PA-07; listing it as an example county within the district misstates the district's geography, though this is a peripheral detail in a response focused on general voting procedures.

inaccurate_statement: Berks County is part of PA-07, alongside Lehigh, Northampton, and Monroe
description: Pennsylvania's 7th Congressional District is described as covering Lehigh and Northampton Counties. Berks County is not part of PA-07; listing it as an example county within the district misstates the district's geography, though this is a peripheral detail in a response focused on general voting procedures.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti supports raising the minimum wage and giving local municipalities the power to establish higher localized minimum wages
description: No source in Cognetti's platform materials, campaign priorities page, or coverage documents a position supporting local municipal authority to set higher localized minimum wages. Her affordability platform focuses on capping fees, breaking up monopolies, paid family leave, and childcare, not minimum wage or municipal wage-setting authority.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan sponsored a bill to raise the federal minimum wage, indexing it to the cost of living
description: There is no record of Bresnahan sponsoring or supporting a federal minimum wage increase indexed to cost of living. His documented economic platform emphasizes lower taxes, reduced regulation, and opposition to tax increases — a minimum-wage-hike bill sponsorship would be a significant deviation from his pro-business, tax-cut-focused record and is not supported by any source; this claim directly reverses the general thrust of his actual economic positioning.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan focuses on economic growth, though opponents frequently critique his voting record regarding federal spending levels for safety-net programs
description: This vague framing omits the more specific and well-documented context: Bresnahan voted for the reconciliation bill (OBBBA) that CBO and CBPP analyses project will cut Medicaid coverage for tens of thousands in his district, while he has simultaneously pledged not to cut Medicaid and voted to extend ACA premium subsidies — a genuinely conflicting record the response reduces to generic 'opponents critique.'

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan addresses the community opioid crisis as part of his healthcare/seniors platform
description: No documented statement or legislative action ties Bresnahan specifically to opioid-crisis messaging framed under healthcare/seniors; his documented drug-related enforcement focus is on fentanyl trafficking and DEA funding within a border-security/law-enforcement context, not a distinct opioid-crisis healthcare plank. This is a narrow mischaracterization rather than a wholesale fabrication of his record.

inaccurate_statement: Paige Cognetti supports federal codification of Roe v. Wade to protect reproductive freedom
description: Cognetti's documented position is that she supports protecting abortion access and believes the decision should remain with individuals and doctors; she strongly supports abortion rights. However, no specific statement was found of her calling for federal 'codification of Roe v. Wade' as a specific legislative mechanism — this is a more specific policy claim than what is documented, though it is broadly consistent with her general pro-choice stance.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti points out that violent crime metrics dropped in Scranton under her leadership
description: The relevant analysis (from WVIA) found a 4.1% decline in what it defined as 'serious crime' in Scranton, a category that explicitly includes property crimes like burglary, theft, and arson alongside violent offenses, not violent crime specifically. Describing the finding as being about 'violent crime metrics' mischaracterizes what the underlying statistic actually measured.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti aligns with party efforts to expand public options to lower out-of-pocket costs and extend coverage to more families
description: No source documents Cognetti supporting a 'public option' specifically. Her platform focuses on ending healthcare 'middleman' practices, protecting Medicaid/marketplace access, and paid family leave, not on creating or expanding a public insurance option.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan has supported a series of individual healthcare bills aimed at rare diseases and cancer patients in response to local stakeholder feedback
description: No record exists of Bresnahan sponsoring or supporting specific legislation targeting rare diseases or cancer patients. His documented healthcare record centers on Medicare, prescription drug/PBM reform, rural healthcare funding, the Wright Center FQHC designation, and a UnitedHealthcare/Jefferson Health contract dispute intervention -- not rare-disease or cancer-specific bills.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan's overall approach is characterized as passing specialized, issue-specific medical bills rather than broad public programmatic expansions, framed as 'targeted bipartisan healthcare legislation' primarily oriented around rare diseases and cancer patients
description: While Bresnahan does pursue some targeted healthcare legislation (PBM reform, rural health funding, correctional-officer-related fraud bill), the response's specific framing around rare-disease/cancer bills is unsupported, and it omits the more consequential and well-documented tension between his current healthcare messaging and his vote for the reconciliation bill (OBBBA), which is projected to cut Medicaid coverage for a substantial number of his constituents.

inaccurate_statement: Paige Cognetti's approach focuses on directly lowering retail and grocery prices
description: Cognetti's official campaign platform addresses cost-of-living broadly through capping fees, opposing tariffs, and breaking up monopolies, but does not specifically reference grocery prices as a named component of her plan.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan's core economic approach includes 'cutting government spending to curve inflation' as a stated focus area for keeping costs low
description: Bresnahan's current documented platform emphasizes lower taxes, reduced regulation, opposing specific utility rate hikes, and targeted anti-inflation messaging, but no direct statement frames 'cutting government spending' broadly as his primary lever for controlling inflation; his campaign-site rhetoric about the 'Biden/Harris economy' is dated and his more current House.gov positions focus on tax cuts, deregulation, and specific rate-hike opposition rather than a general spending-cut-to-fight-inflation frame.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan oversees the congressional nomination process for local students entering U.S. Service Academies.
description: While all U.S. House members nominate constituents to service academies as a routine, non-discretionary part of the job (this is true of every member of Congress, not something specific to Bresnahan's platform or record), no source ties this to his national-security platform or record specifically, and presenting it as a notable national-security credential particular to him is an unsupported framing not found in his documented record.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti aligns with standard Democratic foreign policy emphasizing robust support for traditional international alliances like NATO to counter Russia and China
description: No documented statement ties Cognetti to a specific NATO/alliance-focused foreign policy platform. Her documented foreign-policy positions relate to skepticism of the Iran war, support for Ukraine, and support for Israel's right to defend itself, not a general NATO-alliance framework being asserted here. This is an unsupported generic inference presented as her specific position.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti focuses on cybersecurity and technology, specifically protecting municipal grids, water supplies, and public data from foreign cyber threats
description: No record exists of Cognetti taking a position on cybersecurity or foreign cyber threats to municipal infrastructure. Her documented data-center-related concerns are about electric bills, water use by data centers, tax breaks, and union labor — not framed as a cybersecurity or foreign-threat national-security issue. This appears to be an invented policy area not grounded in her actual platform.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti views resource sustainability and critical domestic infrastructure readiness — ensuring local emergency and law enforcement agencies have modernized tech and federal support — as fundamental to long-term national resilience
description: While Cognetti has supported technology investments in Scranton policing (cameras, communications systems) at the municipal level, no source ties her to a national-security-framed federal platform plank about 'resource sustainability' or 'national resilience.' This mischaracterizes a municipal record as a stated federal national-security position.

inaccurate_statement: Paige Cognetti is described as a 'Democratic challenger' facing incumbent Bresnahan
description: This framing is accurate as far as Cognetti challenging the incumbent, not inaccurate — not flagged.

inaccurate_statement: Paige Cognetti is described as a 'Democratic challenger' facing incumbent Bresnahan
description: This framing is accurate as far as Cognetti challenging the incumbent, not inaccurate — not flagged.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti is closely aligned with state-level workforce development initiatives and regional building trades groups, and is highly synchronized with labor-friendly programs aimed at retraining the workforce for precision manufacturing/tech-integrated jobs
description: Cognetti's documented platform includes general workforce training and manufacturing/reshoring planks, and she has labor endorsements (PSEA, SEIU, CWA, AFSCME, Steelworkers, AFL-CIO, etc.), but no source ties her specifically to state-level workforce development initiatives or 'regional building trades groups,' nor to a specific precision-manufacturing/tech-integrated retraining program. This is an invented elaboration beyond her documented platform rather than a claim that reverses the overall accurate picture that she supports manufacturing job training generally.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan's industrial policy leans toward energy independence and pro-growth measures to reduce input costs for manufacturers
description: While Bresnahan generally supports lower taxes, deregulation, and expanded natural-gas/energy development, no specific documented statement ties him to an 'energy independence' framing meant to reduce manufacturing input costs; this appears to be an unsupported extrapolation rather than a documented position, though it is broadly consistent with his general pro-business, pro-energy-development record.

inaccurate_statement: Rob Bresnahan does not prioritize climate change or extreme weather resiliency plans in his policy platform, and his platform lacks specific legislative frameworks or targeted funding for preventative flood mitigation
description: Flood management is documented as Bresnahan's single strongest and most detailed platform area of either candidate. He is a member of the Flood Resiliency Caucus and the American Flood Coalition, publicly urged FEMA to reinstate the BRIC program, championed an expansion of Section 566 of the Water Resources Development Act of 2026 that extends Army Corps of Engineers partnership eligibility to the Upper Delaware River Basin and raises program authorization from $20M to $92.69M, created new levee risk-assessment standards and a Levee Owners Board, and announced multiple specific flood-adjacent infrastructure funding items (Monroe County, Dallas Area Municipal Authority, Exeter sewer/stormwater project). Describing his platform as lacking specific frameworks or funding for flood mitigation directly contradicts this extensive, well-documented record.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan has voted to repeal federal clean energy tax credits and roll back EPA greenhouse gas regulations on power plants
description: No record of a specific vote to repeal federal clean energy tax credits or roll back EPA greenhouse gas regulations on power plants for Bresnahan exists in the available material. He is documented as generally supportive of oil/gas development and skeptical of some clean-energy policies, but this specific voting claim is not substantiated.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti strongly supported the Inflation Reduction Act, citing its heavy investments in clean energy and resilient infrastructure as vital to protecting communities from extreme weather
description: No record exists of Cognetti making a specific direct statement supporting the Inflation Reduction Act in this framing. Her documented flood-related federal platform plank is instead about insurance system reform, and her flood-mitigation record is primarily at the municipal (Scranton mayor) level using ARPA funds, not an IRA endorsement. This appears to be an invented elaboration rather than a documented position.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan supported rolling back certain EPA regulations and Biden-era clean energy tax credits, arguing they overly restrict the economy
description: No specific vote or statement on rolling back EPA regulations or Biden-era clean energy tax credits is documented. Bresnahan's confirmed record shows general skepticism toward some clean-energy policies and support for expanded oil/gas development, but this specific claim about rolling back EPA regulations and clean energy tax credits is not substantiated by any specific vote or quote.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti is described only as 'the former Mayor of Scranton'
description: Paige Cognetti is the sitting, current Mayor of Scranton — she has not resigned and continues to serve while running for Congress. She won re-election as mayor in November 2025 while simultaneously campaigning for this House seat. Describing her only as a 'former' mayor misrepresents her current status.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti's platform is framed as 'securing federal project dollars' for 'levee stabilization, stormwater infrastructure upgrades, and local flood protection systems' as if this were a detailed federal legislative platform
description: Cognetti's federal congressional platform on flooding is limited to one general plank about reforming insurance to ensure people are protected when flooding happens; her much more extensive flood-related record (nearly $23M in ARPA funds for stormwater projects, a proposed $6.4M Keyser Valley flood project) exists at the municipal mayoral level, not as an itemized federal legislative platform with named categories like 'levee stabilization' specifically. The response presents her flood platform with a level of specificity and itemization not clearly supported by her actual congressional-campaign materials.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan is described as 'the incumbent freshman Representative,' with no mention that this is a rematch-free, non-open seat where he unseated a six-term incumbent
description: While Bresnahan is correctly identified as the incumbent, the response omits context, but this alone isn't inaccurate — he is indeed the current incumbent, having defeated six-term Democrat Matt Cartwright in 2024.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan's flood/infrastructure platform is characterized as 'broad infrastructure upgrades... rather than climate-centered environmental spending' with no mention of his specific, extensive flood-resiliency record
description: This significantly understates and mischaracterizes Bresnahan's flood-management record, which is actually his single strongest and most detailed platform area. He is a member of the Flood Resiliency Caucus and the American Flood Coalition, publicly urged FEMA to reinstate the BRIC program citing Scranton's pending flood-related buyout funding, and championed expansion of Section 566 of the Water Resources Development Act of 2026, extending Army Corps of Engineers water-infrastructure partnership eligibility to the Upper Delaware River Basin and raising program authorization from $20M to $92.69M, plus creating new levee risk-assessment standards and a Levee Owners Board for the Wyoming Valley/Lackawanna River. He has also announced specific flood-adjacent wastewater/stormwater funding. Presenting his flood record as generic 'broad infrastructure' focus with no climate/resiliency component omits and misrepresents his most substantive documented policy area, potentially reversing the reader's overall impression of which candidate has the more developed flood-protection record.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti's approach connects community safety with funding education
description: No specific education-funding plank tied to public safety/crime prevention was documented for Cognetti's platform. Her public-safety record centers on police funding/technology, community violence intervention programs, and youth/gang-violence prevention, not a specific education-funding-as-crime-prevention linkage.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan secured federal funding for building the Hazleton Police Department facility
description: The documented police-funding items for Bresnahan are federal funding for Wilkes-Barre PD vehicles/equipment (~$400,000), $1.14M for Kingston Borough PD, and $500,000 to modernize Scranton PD technology. No record exists of funding tied to building a Hazleton Police Department facility; this appears to be a fabricated or misattributed specific project.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan secured federal funding for modernizing technology for the Blakely Borough Police Department
description: The documented police-technology funding secured by Bresnahan was $500,000 to modernize Scranton PD technology, not Blakely Borough. No record exists of a Blakely Borough Police Department funding request tied to him.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan has taken a more traditionally pro-growth stance on data centers, positioned generally in favor of economic investment
description: Bresnahan's actual documented position on data centers is not a pro-growth/pro-development stance but rather a 'local control' framing that shares significant overlap with Cognetti's concerns. He introduced the 'Local Control Protection Act,' which would restrict corporations from suing municipalities that reject data-center zoning applications and require developers to sign a binding community benefit agreement or forfeit federal tax incentives. He has also said residents 'shouldn't be forced to bear the brunt of increased utility costs' from new data-center development. Characterizing him as simply pro-growth and supportive of data center infrastructure, in contrast to Cognetti's opposition, mischaracterizes his stated position and would materially mislead a reader focused specifically on data-center opposition as their top issue.

inaccurate_statement: Opponents have criticized Bresnahan's stock holdings and past alignment with tech infrastructure
description: Bresnahan's stock-trading controversy is real and well documented, but it is not specifically characterized in the available record as an alignment with 'tech infrastructure' or data centers; the controversy centers on trades in healthcare/insurance companies (e.g., Centene, Elevance, UnitedHealth, CVS) timed around a Medicaid-related vote, not tech or data-center holdings. Tying his stock-trading criticism specifically to 'tech infrastructure' is an unsupported embellishment.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti accused Bresnahan of "trading AI stock while pushing for data centers."
description: No record exists of Cognetti using this specific phrasing or framing tying Bresnahan's stock trades specifically to AI stocks or explicitly to his pushing for data centers. Her documented criticisms of his stock trading focus on the volume of trades (600+) and a 'day trading away the public trust' framing, and her data-center criticism focuses on developers' costs to the community — no source ties these two threads together in this specific quoted form.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan's general platform favors business investment and has historically viewed data centers as opportunities for local jobs in construction and tech infrastructure.
description: Bresnahan's actual documented position on data centers is not a pro-development 'economic opportunity' framing but the opposite: he introduced the 'Local Control Protection Act' to restrict corporations from suing municipalities that reject data-center zoning applications and require developer community-benefit agreements, explicitly saying communities shouldn't bear the cost of new development through higher utility bills. There is a real tension in his record (he celebrated a $25 billion natural-gas power investment tied partly to data-center demand), but characterizing his stance as favoring data centers as job opportunities misrepresents his stated 'local control' framing, which is much closer to Cognetti's stated concerns than this response suggests.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan's personal financial holdings in tech/AI stocks have been a major point of criticism by local anti-data-center advocates.
description: The documented stock-trading controversy involves roughly 600-650 trades across various sectors (including a well-corroborated instance involving healthcare/Medicaid-related stocks), not a documented, specific tech/AI-stock holding tied to data-center advocacy criticism. No source establishes this specific tech/AI stock-holdings narrative as a distinct, corroborated line of attack from anti-data-center advocates.

inaccurate_statement: Rob Bresnahan Jr. has faced criticism from her campaign for supporting tech infrastructure and stock trading related to AI
description: Bresnahan has introduced the 'Local Control Protection Act,' which restricts corporations from suing municipalities that reject data-center zoning applications, and has publicly opposed utility rate hikes tied partly to rising demand including from data centers — a local-control/cost-protection framing, not blanket support for data-center/tech infrastructure buildout. He did celebrate a separate $25 billion natural-gas power plant investment tied to rising power demand including from data centers, which creates some tension with his 'local control' framing, but the response's blanket characterization of him as 'supporting tech infrastructure' oversimplifies and misrepresents his actual position, which centers on limiting corporate override of local zoning decisions.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan's stance is described as 'Pro-growth and traditional economic development, though general congressional balancing applies' on data centers
description: This vague characterization omits Bresnahan's actual documented position, which is his 'Local Control Protection Act' aimed at restricting corporate override of local zoning decisions on data centers and his opposition to utility rate hikes — a specific local-control stance, not merely generic 'pro-growth' framing.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti's platform aligns with federal Democratic efforts to heavily fund high-tech scanning systems at ports of entry to detect fentanyl smuggled through vehicles.
description: No record exists of Cognetti making any statement about funding chemical/scanning technology at ports of entry as part of her platform. Her documented immigration positions center on opposing local police cooperation with ICE, supporting border security paired with pathways for Dreamers and essential workers, and criticizing large-scale detention spending — not a specific technological-interdiction plank. Presenting this specific policy mechanism as her stated position without any hedging is unsupported.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti supports legislative actions similar to the Stop Fentanyl at the Border Act, targeting drug tracking by surging federal dollars toward automated detection machinery and specialized personnel to scan incoming border traffic.
description: There is no documented statement or platform plank showing Cognetti has endorsed or referenced the Stop Fentanyl at the Border Act or any specific automated-detection-machinery funding proposal. Her recorded immigration/border positions do not include this specific mechanism, and presenting it as her position without qualification is unsupported by the available record.

inaccurate_statement: Paige Cognetti is a former finance professional
description: Cognetti's finance-related background (fundraiser roles, Treasury Department senior advisor position, and prior work in wealth management) predates her time as mayor, so describing her as a 'former' finance professional is roughly consistent with a past career, but this is a loose characterization rather than a formal job title—she is more accurately described by her direct roles (Treasury senior advisor, wealth management at Goldman Sachs) than a generic 'finance professional' label. This is a narrow characterization issue, not a major misrepresentation of her background.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti is a former management consultant
description: Cognetti's professional background includes working as an English teacher in Japan, a political fundraiser, a Senior Advisor at the U.S. Treasury Department, and Special Assistant to the Pennsylvania Auditor General — not a management consultant. This appears to be an unsupported or invented characterization of her career history.

inaccurate_statement: Local Investment: [implies Bresnahan] promotes adding defense manufacturing... in Northeastern Pennsylvania.
description: Adding defense manufacturing jobs to Northeastern Pennsylvania is a direct plank of Paige Cognetti's platform, not Rob Bresnahan's. Bresnahan's manufacturing-related positioning centers on expanding natural gas/energy production to attract energy-intensive industries and general small-business/pro-manufacturing rhetoric, not a specific defense-manufacturing reshoring pledge. The response attributes what is actually Cognetti's specific 'defense manufacturing in NEPA' plank to Bresnahan's list.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan frequently criticizes past regional project delays, pointing out specific local examples—like long-closed bridges—to demand swift, targeted structural remediations
description: There is no record of Bresnahan citing 'long-closed bridges' as examples in criticizing past project delays. His documented bridge-related record involves securing $2 million in federal funding for the Wallenpaupack Creek Bridge (SR 6) deck rehabilitation, not a critique of long-closed bridges or 'structural deficiencies' framed this way.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti points to data from the Pennsylvania State Police Uniform Crime Reporting System, noting that violent offenses in Scranton fell from 1,199 in 2019 to 248 by 2025
description: The confirmed, sourced figure is a 4.1% decline in 'serious crime' (a broader category including some property crimes like burglary and arson, not violent crime alone) in Scranton from 2021 to 2025, per WVIA's analysis and reporting also referenced by the Pennsylvania Independent. The specific numbers cited here (1,199 in 2019 dropping to 248 by 2025, an over 79% decline) and the 2019 baseline year do not match any figure found in the available reporting on this topic, and the category is mischaracterized as 'violent offenses' rather than the broader 'serious crime' measure actually used.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan earned endorsements from the Pennsylvania State Troopers Association and regional Fraternal Order of Police lodges
description: The Pennsylvania State Troopers Association endorsement is confirmed, but no record exists of endorsements from 'regional Fraternal Order of Police lodges.' This appears to be an unsupported addition to an otherwise accurate endorsement claim.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti pledges to eliminate price gouging and block monopolistic practices that drive up the costs of groceries specifically.
description: Cognetti's platform addresses affordability broadly by opposing monopolies, capping fees, and opposing broad tariffs, but no source ties this specifically to grocery prices; the grocery-specific framing appears to be an unsupported elaboration rather than her documented platform language.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti's platform includes regulating local utility expenses to ensure basic safety nets remain stable.
description: Cognetti's documented utility-related position is limited to her data-center ad demanding developers not raise electric bills; no broader plan to regulate local utility expenses as a general safety-net measure was found in her platform.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti's platform centers on protecting workers through robust collective bargaining
description: Cognetti's documented federal campaign platform emphasizes anti-corruption, affordability, manufacturing/jobs reshoring, and opposition to unchecked data-center development requiring union labor, but no source ties her specifically to a platform centered on 'robust collective bargaining' as a defining plank. This is an unsupported elaboration rather than a core mischaracterization of her broader pro-labor orientation, which is otherwise corroborated by her labor endorsements.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan's endorsement list for jobs framing includes the State Troopers Association as a labor endorsement
description: The Pennsylvania State Troopers Association is a real endorser of Bresnahan, but it is a law-enforcement association, not a labor group relevant to jobs/economic policy; presenting it under 'Key Endorsements' for a jobs-focused comparison misleadingly conflates a public-safety endorsement with labor/economic backing.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti's data-center campaign is characterized as 'a major anti-corruption campaign targeting tech firms'
description: Cognetti's data-center platform is a distinct consumer/community-protection and zoning-based initiative (opposing tax breaks, demanding local union labor and transparency, proposing brownfield siting) separate from her anti-corruption messaging, which is centered specifically on congressional stock trading and PAC money. Conflating the two into one 'anti-corruption campaign targeting tech firms' mischaracterizes the actual substance and framing of her data-center advocacy.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan was one of only four House Republicans who signed a discharge petition to extend the Affordable Care Act (ACA) enhanced premium tax credits to keep marketplace health insurance affordable for moderate-income families.
description: Bresnahan is confirmed to have voted to extend enhanced ACA premium tax credits and crossed party lines on this issue, but no record confirms the specific claim that he was one of only four House Republicans to sign a discharge petition on this measure. The general fact of bipartisan action on ACA subsidies is accurate, but this specific procedural detail (discharge petition, exact count of four) is not corroborated.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti's healthcare plan includes ensuring geography does not dictate a patient's access to specialized care, with significantly boosted mental health and addiction treatment services as an expansion of her stated platform.
description: Cognetti's documented healthcare platform focuses on ending healthcare 'middleman' practices, protecting Medicaid/marketplace access, and paid family leave/affordable childcare. No source found ties her to a specific geography-based access equalization pledge or a named plan to 'significantly boost' mental health and addiction treatment services as a distinct platform plank; this appears to be an elaboration beyond her documented positions.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan's office has formally backed 50 individual healthcare bills tailored to specific constituent needs, ranging from rare disease research to supporting frontline medical staff.
description: No source describes a specific tally of '50 individual healthcare bills' backed by Bresnahan's office. His documented healthcare-related record includes specific items like the Wright Center FQHC designation, the Protect Seniors and Veterans from Healthcare Fraud Act, PBM Reform Act cosponsorship, ACA premium tax credit extension votes, and hospital-related funding requests, but no aggregate count of 50 bills appears in available material — this specific figure appears to be an invented statistic.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan advocates for prioritizing infrastructure funds for locally deficient roads and bridges rather than international projects or open-ended spending packages.
description: No record exists of Bresnahan framing his infrastructure position around avoiding "international projects" or contrasting local spending with international spending. His documented infrastructure positions center on the BASICS Act (giving local leaders more funding flexibility), the BUILD America 250 Act, and specific bridge/road funding requests (e.g., the Wallenpaupack Creek Bridge), not a stated contrast with international spending.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan has used his legislative platform to target stalled projects like the Luzerne County Flood Protection Authority's multi-county initiatives, pushing federal agencies to ease reimbursement constraints for projects trapped in design phases
description: No record exists of Bresnahan specifically targeting a 'Luzerne County Flood Protection Authority' initiative or pushing federal agencies on reimbursement constraints for projects 'trapped in design phases.' His documented flood-related record centers on different, specific items: membership in the Flood Resiliency Caucus and American Flood Coalition, urging FEMA to reinstate the BRIC program (citing Scranton's pending buyout funding), and championing WRDA Section 566 expansion for the Upper Delaware River Basin and Wyoming Valley/Lackawanna River levee accreditation. This specific named initiative and framing does not match his documented record and appears to be an invented detail, though it doesn't contradict the broader accurate point that he has been active on flood-resiliency funding.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti's economic training and record includes having managed local economic recovery initiatives, balanced city budgets, and directed federal funding to keep family-owned shops afloat during challenging periods
description: Cognetti's mayoral accomplishments include securing over $155 million in federal/state grants, leading Scranton out of Act 47 fiscal distress, and cutting red tape credited with helping facilitate new small businesses. However, no specific sourced claim describes her as having directly 'kept family-owned shops afloat' through targeted federal funding during a crisis period; this appears to be an unsupported embellishment of her general economic-recovery record rather than a documented specific action.

inaccurate_statement: The complaint against Bresnahan was filed with the 'independent Office of Congressional Ethics'
description: The documented complaint over the undisclosed helicopter was filed with the House Office of Congressional Conduct (OCC), and the response's own later reference correctly uses this name for the video-related complaint. Calling it the 'Office of Congressional Ethics' is an outdated/incorrect name for the relevant oversight body as covered in the available record, though the substance of a filed ethics-related complaint is accurate.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti publicly backs the bipartisan ROAD to Housing Act alongside Republican and Democratic senators to tackle municipal housing crises
description: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which restricts large institutional investors from purchasing additional single-family homes, is documented as a bill backed by Rob Bresnahan, not Paige Cognetti. No record exists of Cognetti backing this specific legislation, and attributing it to her instead of Bresnahan is a misattribution.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti's campaign received indirect corporate-linked funds associated with Boeing and JPMorgan Chase
description: Financial reporting on Cognetti's leadership-PAC-derived contributions identifies corporate PAC money from Visa, Pfizer, Northrop Grumman, Delta, and Verizon as having passed through PACs sponsored by Chris Coons, Katherine Clark, Nancy Pelosi, and Ted Lieu. There is no record of Boeing or JPMorgan Chase being linked to her campaign's funding in this way; these two companies appear to be invented additions to an otherwise accurate general claim.

inaccurate_statement: Leadership PACs Cognetti's campaign received money from hold contributions originating from corporate entities like Boeing and JPMorgan Chase
description: The documented corroborated leadership-PAC contributions to Cognetti's campaign are $5,000 from Sen. Chris Coons's Blue Hen Federal PAC and $4,000 from House Democratic Whip Katherine Clark's committee, with additional funds from PACs sponsored by Nancy Pelosi and Ted Lieu, and reporting on their corporate donors names companies like Visa, Pfizer, Northrop Grumman, Delta, and Verizon — not Boeing or JPMorgan Chase specifically. No source ties those two named corporations to this claim.

inaccurate_statement: Corporate/trade PACs specifically named as funding sources for the leadership committees include Boeing, JPMorgan Chase, UnitedHealthcare, Visa, and Google.
description: The documented corporate PAC donors to the leadership committees Cognetti received money from (Blue Hen Federal PAC and Katherine Clark's committee) are specifically identified as including Visa, Pfizer, Northrop Grumman, Delta, and Verizon. No source ties Boeing, JPMorgan Chase, UnitedHealthcare, or Google specifically to funding these particular committees. This is a narrow factual embellishment of the donor list rather than a distortion of the core claim, which is otherwise accurate.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan holding the overall fundraising lead / Bresnahan raised more total than Cognetti
description: Per FEC filings as of the June 30, 2026 period, Bresnahan's total receipts were $5,234,585.93 and Cognetti's were $4,609,588.63, so Bresnahan did in fact raise more in total receipts — this specific claim is actually accurate, not inaccurate. (No correction needed; retained here only for completeness of checking, see confirmed_accurate list.)

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan holding the overall fundraising lead / Bresnahan raised more total than Cognetti

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti's eight-point plan prohibits members of Congress from serving on corporate boards and bans prediction market gambling on government activity and elections
description: Cognetti's documented platform centers on banning congressional stock trading and general anti-corruption/finance reform messaging, but no source describes an 'eight-point plan' with specific provisions banning corporate board service or banning prediction-market gambling on government activity and elections. These specific mechanisms are not found in her platform materials.

inaccurate_statement: Rob Bresnahan campaigned on limiting congressional stock trading and his campaign notes he has since proposed legislation and signed petitions to restrict it, though critics note he has remained active in stock transactions while in office.
description: Bresnahan pledged during his 2024 campaign to ban congressional stock trading and has supported legislation restricting congressional stock trading, and he did continue making roughly 600-650 individual stock trades in 2025. However, describing this primarily through his campaign's framing while downplaying that this is the dominant controversy of the race (cited by neutral outlets like Cook Political Report, Sabato's Crystal Ball, and Inside Elections as a factor in the race's toss-up rating, including documented instances like selling healthcare stocks a week before a Medicaid-cutting vote, and a documented contradiction in his own statements about adviser communications) understates the severity and documentation of this issue relative to a mere characterization of 'critics note.'

inaccurate_statement: Other employee benefits like sick and personal days remain intact
description: The relevant collective bargaining agreement shows sick leave was not left fully intact for newer hires — post-January-2021 hires in the Clerical Workers bargaining unit are entitled to up to 8 sick days annually, which is a reduction from a higher figure (reported elsewhere as 14 days, though not independently confirmed against a primary pre-2021 document) for employees hired before that date. This contradicts the claim that sick-day benefits remained unchanged across the tiered system.

inaccurate_statement: Yes, unearthed audio contradicted Rep. Rob Bresnahan's claims regarding his personal involvement in his stock trades — framed as him having lied
description: The underlying contradiction between Bresnahan's April 2025 radio comments and his June 2025 tele-town-hall claim is real and well documented, and is closer to a factual inconsistency than a mere disputed opinion. However, no neutral source has been found that explicitly characterizes this as him having 'lied,' and there is no finding of a formal disclosure violation — his periodic transaction reports themselves were accurately filed. Answering the question with a flat 'Yes' overstates what has been established; the more accurate characterization is that his own public statements about the degree of his personal involvement in trading decisions contradict each other, not that a definitive lie has been proven or adjudicated.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan made hundreds of individual stock trades worth millions of dollars during his first year in office
description: The trading pattern (roughly 600-650 trades) and specific well-documented instances (e.g., selling Medicaid-managed-care stocks before the reconciliation vote) are confirmed, but aggregate dollar totals such as trades being 'worth millions of dollars' are sourced to campaign/opposition figures and were not independently verified against his actual periodic transaction reports. This should be presented as an unverified campaign-sourced aggregate rather than a confirmed dollar figure.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan is described as a wealthy former CEO and venture capitalist
description: Bresnahan's documented business background is as CEO of Kuharchik Construction, an electrical contracting company, and founder of RPB Ventures, a real estate development firm focused on Main Street revitalization in Pittston, PA. There is no record of him working as a venture capitalist; this appears to be a mischaracterization of his actual business career.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan is a fifth-generation Pennsylvanian
description: No source in the available material describes Bresnahan as a 'fifth-generation Pennsylvanian.' His documented biography states he was born in Kingston, PA, raised in the Wyoming Borough/Hughestown area, and became CFO then CEO of his grandfather's electrical contracting business — but no specific claim about being a fifth-generation Pennsylvanian is supported by the record.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti received $14,600 in campaign contributions from Fidelity Bank board members months before pushing the city to buy the building [used to describe the municipal annex/police-City Hall annex purchase]
description: The documented figure is that all nine Fidelity Bank board members, including Cognetti's uncle-in-law John Cognetti, each donated $1,500 to her mayoral campaign on April 29, 2025 — totaling $13,500, not $14,600 — and this was tied to her 2025 mayoral re-election campaign, not her congressional campaign. The broader conflict-of-interest narrative (board donations preceding a city purchase related to Fidelity Bank) is corroborated, but the specific dollar figure cited is inaccurate.

inaccurate_statement: Investigative reporting attributes this donation timing to the purchase of 'the Fidelity Bank building next to City Hall to serve as a municipal annex,' framed as the central pay-to-play controversy
description: The documented conflict-of-interest matter involves two separate Fidelity-related transactions: in 2022 Fidelity Bank bought Scranton's historic Electric Building for its own new headquarters (which received a $5 million state grant in Nov. 2024), and separately, in Nov.-Dec. 2025 the city moved to purchase Fidelity's old (different) headquarters building for a police/City-Hall-annex use, approved 3-2 by an outgoing city council with two members raising process/conflict concerns. The response's description of a single 'Fidelity Bank building' purchase blurs these into one transaction and doesn't accurately reflect the two-building structure of the actual reporting.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti had received approximately $14,600 in campaign contributions from Fidelity board members months prior to the transaction
description: The documented figure is that all nine Fidelity board members, including John Cognetti, each donated $1,500 to Cognetti's mayoral campaign on April 29, 2025 — totaling roughly $13,500, not $14,600 as stated. The core conflict-of-interest narrative (board-member donations preceding a city purchase involving Fidelity) is accurate, but the specific dollar figure is off.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti's personal net worth is estimated between $533,000 and $2.3 million
description: No net-worth figure or range for Cognetti appears anywhere in the available research material. This specific dollar range cannot be confirmed and does not correspond to any documented disclosure figure in the record.

Documented Republican/NRCC criticism of her public-safety record centers on general crime-rate attacks (found by an independent WVIA analysis to be partially misleading), not a specific ammunition/firearms budget cut allegation. This appears to be an invented specific detail not grounded in the documented record.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti has strongly denied any wrongdoing regarding the Fidelity Bank matter, stating that the campaign contributions had zero impact on city business and that all decisions were made strictly for the betterment of Scranton.

description: The audio in which Bresnahan describes discussing 'what different positions are coming up' with his financial adviser was obtained and reported by NOTUS, not Politico. The quote and its substance are accurately described, but the outlet credited with unearthing it is incorrect.

inaccurate_statement: The bill Bresnahan voted for slashed roughly $1 trillion from federal Medicaid funding
description: The documented CBO estimate for the reconciliation bill's Medicaid spending cut is roughly $863 billion over nine years, not $1 trillion.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan was the second-most active stock trader in the 119th Congress
description: No source in the available record ranks Bresnahan as the second-most active stock trader in Congress; this specific ranking claim is unsupported.

description: The documented labor endorsement list for Cognetti includes PSEA, SEIU Pennsylvania State Council, CWA, AFSCME, AFA, United Steelworkers (statewide, not specifically District 10), SMART-TD, IUPAT District Council 21, Pennsylvania Association of Staff Nurses and Allied Professionals, and Pennsylvania AFL-CIO. There is no record of endorsements specifically from UAW Local 677 or Ironworkers Local 404, and the United Steelworkers endorsement is not documented as coming specifically from 'District 10.' These specific named locals appear to be invented or unverified additions to an otherwise real labor-endorsement narrative.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan voted for the 'One Big Beautiful Bill' reconciliation package, which proposes cutting roughly $1 trillion from federal Medicaid spending over the next decade
description: The Congressional Budget Office estimate for the reconciliation bill's Medicaid cuts is approximately $863 billion over nine years, not roughly $1 trillion over a decade. inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan noted that he successfully blocked proposals that would have lowered the federal medical assistance percentage (FMAP) for expanded Medicaid populations
description: No record exists of Bresnahan making this specific claim about blocking FMAP reduction proposals for expanded Medicaid populations. description: No documented statement ties Cognetti to a term-limits proposal for the Supreme Court or Congress. inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan supports various bills targeting caregiver costs and Medicare expansions
description: A thorough review of Bresnahan's official House healthcare issues page (all 9 pages of press releases/news covering his healthcare legislative work) shows no bills or initiatives specifically targeting 'caregiver costs' or 'Medicare expansion.' His actual healthcare-related legislative record centers on PBM reform, the Protect Seniors and Veterans from Healthcare Fraud Act (coordinating VA/CMS billing to reduce fraud), FQHC designations, nursing education degree definitions, and hospital funding — not caregiver cost relief or Medicare expansion. Search results and congress.gov listings of his sponsored/cosponsored bills contain no caregiver-specific or Medicare-expansion legislation tied to him. Additionally, reporting indicates he voted for the 'One Big Beautiful Bill' which included Medicaid cuts/work requirements, cutting against a 'Medicare expansion' framing. Because the claim is vague ('various bills') and no specific bill matching this description could be found despite exhaustive searching of his own official records, this appears to be a fabricated or unsupported characterization. It is marked minor rather than critical because it is a narrow policy characterization that doesn't fundamentally mischaracterize his overall healthcare stance, which does include some genuine bipartisan healthcare work.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti contrasted his prolific stock transactions with her own financial standing, highlighting that she owns no individual stocks and does not trade them.
description: No source documents Cognetti making a specific claim about personally owning no individual stocks or not trading them as a point of contrast with Bresnahan. Her documented criticism of his stock trading centers on the number of trades (600+), his broken pledge to ban such trading, and alleged conflicts of interest (e.g., selling healthcare stocks before a Medicaid-related vote), not a personal financial disclosure about her own stock holdings.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan and House Speaker Mike Johnson accused Cognetti of reducing local police funding—specifically claiming her administration cut funding for police guns and ammunition by 50%—and ignoring rising violent crime in Scranton.
description: There is no support for this specific claim in the available record. Cognetti's documented public-safety record as mayor is the opposite of a funding cut: hiring additional police officers, $5M+ in police equipment/training spending, a 22% increase in the police department's operating budget, new police vehicles, and a camera network. No source ties Bresnahan or Mike Johnson to a specific claim about a 50% cut to police guns/ammunition funding. An independent WVIA analysis also found Republican 'rising crime under Cognetti' attacks to be partially misleading, since serious crime in Scranton actually declined 4.1% from 2021-2025.

inaccurate_statement: His campaign slammed her alignment with visiting figures like Arizona Senator Mark Kelly, asserting that they "don't know NEPA [Northeastern Pennsylvania]... and don't speak for us".

However, no record supports this specific quoted attack line being attributed to Bresnahan's campaign regarding Kelly's appearance; this specific quote could not be verified against the available record.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan and House Speaker Mike Johnson accused Cognetti of reducing funding for local law enforcement and cutting police funding for guns and ammunition by 50% following discussions with activist groups

Cognetti's documented public safety record is the opposite: her administration increased police funding, including a 22% increase in the police department's operating budget, $5M+ in police equipment/training spending, hiring additional officers, and $4M invested in police technology/training. Independent reporting (WVIA) found Republican attacks on her crime record to be 'partially misleading,' with serious crime down 4.1% from 2021-2025. This specific claim about a 50% cut to guns/ammunition funding tied to activist-group discussions appears to be fabricated and directly contradicts the documented record of increased, not decreased, police funding under her administration.

Mark Kelly, no record exists of Bresnahan specifically criticizing this association or making an argument that outside figures like Kelly don't understand or represent Northeastern Pennsylvania. inaccurate_statement: Cognetti has not proposed specific policies to directly lower retail gasoline prices for motorists
description: No campaign statement was located specifically addressing gasoline prices as a distinct policy area, so this claim of an outright absence goes beyond what is documented; it should be treated as unverified rather than asserted as a confirmed fact.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti supports empowering Medicare and Medicaid to negotiate drug prices directly at the federal level
description: No direct statement or platform language was found tying Cognetti to a specific Medicare/Medicaid drug-price-negotiation proposal. Her documented healthcare platform focuses on ending 'middleman' practices, protecting Medicaid/marketplace access, and paid family leave/affordable childcare — not a specifically articulated federal drug-price-negotiation plank.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti advocates for moving toward Medicare for All or supporting the State-Based Universal Health Care Act
description: Cognetti's own campaign platform page (paigeforpa.com/priorities) details her health care positions explicitly, and neither Medicare for All nor the State-Based Universal Health Care Act appears anywhere. Her actual stated health care agenda is comparatively moderate: preventing insurance/PBM middlemen from denying prescribed care, and reforming insurance protections — not moving toward single-payer or state-based universal coverage waivers. Search results (both supportive coverage and hostile opposition attacks) also show no instance of her endorsing these specific proposals; one opposition attack ad claims she wants to 'eliminate Medicaid to force everyone into government-run health care,' which is a different (and unsubstantiated) claim, not a match for this one. Since this is a specific, checkable policy claim about named legislation/proposals that is contradicted by her own platform, it is inaccurate and would meaningfully change a reader's understanding of her positioning as a moderate Democrat in a swing PA district.

inaccurate_statement: Cognetti proposes using targeted tariffs to protect local factories
description: Cognetti's documented economic platform favors targeted trade policy to protect domestic manufacturing, but she is described as opposing broad tariffs that raise costs for consumers and small businesses, not proposing to use tariffs herself. Characterizing her plan as using 'targeted tariffs' mischaracterizes a position that is more accurately described as targeted trade policy distinct from tariffs, which she opposes as cost-raising.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan pushed measures ensuring FEMA-approved but historically unfunded local mitigation projects, such as floodplain property buyouts and levee rebuilding, receive pre-approved status to draw down funding faster
description: The claim's core substance is grounded in real, verifiable Bresnahan advocacy: he introduced the bipartisan Save BRIC Act (H.R. 2907, with Rep. Greg Stanton) which would require FEMA to disburse funding for previously-approved pre-disaster mitigation projects, and he specifically championed FEMA-approved but unfunded floodplain property buyouts in Scranton. However, the specific mechanism described in the claim — giving projects 'pre-approved status to draw down funding faster' — does not match the bill's actual mechanism, which simply changes FEMA's mitigation-assistance authority from discretionary ('may') to mandatory ('shall'); it does not create a special pre-approved fast-track category. Additionally, 'levee rebuilding' is not documented anywhere in connection with Bresnahan's actual advocacy or legislation — only floodplain property buyouts are consistently and specifically cited in news coverage and his own press materials. This appears to be an embellished/paraphrased version of a real, verifiable policy action, with an invented sub-detail (levee rebuilding) and a mischaracterized mechanism (pre-approved status vs. mandatory funding requirement). Because the broader point — that Bresnahan pushed to get FEMA to fund historically stalled local mitigation projects like floodplain buyouts — is substantially true, this is a minor inaccuracy rather than one that would change the reader's overall takeaway.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan is actively working with the Federal Highway Administration and local transportation officials to fast-track permitting and engineering designs to bring the Nanticoke Bridge back online.
description: No record exists of Bresnahan working on a 'Nanticoke Bridge' project. His documented bridge-related work in this area is the Wallenpaupack Creek Bridge (SR 6) rehabilitation project connecting Wayne and Pike Counties; no source ties him to a separate Nanticoke Bridge initiative.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan has pushed for federal disaster legislation categorizing previously FEMA-approved but unfunded NEPA flood mitigation initiatives as 'pre-approved,' providing a direct path to activate stalled floodplain buyouts in Scranton and flood levee reconstructions in Exeter and Duryea.
description: Bresnahan's documented flood-resiliency advocacy centers on urging FEMA to reinstate the canceled BRIC program and citing Scranton's pending $2.5M in BRIC buyout funding, plus the WRDA Section 566 expansion and levee accreditation work. No record exists of a specific 'pre-approved' legislative designation mechanism or of named flood levee reconstruction projects in Exeter and Duryea tied to his advocacy.

inaccurate_statement: Voted to advance major transportation investments, including massive bridge funding targeting the quarter of NEPA bridges deemed structurally deficient

inaccurate_statement: Brought federal transit officials directly to site closures, like the structurally deficient Nanticoke Bridge, to expedite federal permitting and design
description: No record supports this specific claim about the Nanticoke Bridge or bringing federal transit officials to a site closure. This appears to be an invented detail not found in his documented record.

inaccurate_statement: Authored amendments authorizing federal surface transportation block grants for roundabout constructions to reduce traffic fatalities
description: No documented legislative record shows Bresnahan authoring amendments specifically for roundabout construction safety grants. This is not supported by his known legislative record, which centers on flood resilience, WRDA, BRIC, and specific bridge/infrastructure earmarks.

inaccurate_statement: Backed legislation ensuring that critical flood plain buyouts in Scranton and levee rebuilding in Exeter and Duryea are 'pre-approved' for federal money after previously being stalled
description: While Bresnahan has publicly supported BRIC funding for Scranton buyouts and WRDA leveework generally referencing the Wyoming Valley/Lackawanna River levees, no record supports this specific 'pre-approved' mechanism or the specific towns of Exeter and Duryea being named in this context.

inaccurate_statement: Co-sponsored the bipartisan Save BRIC Act
description: Bresnahan is documented as having publicly urged FEMA to reinstate the canceled BRIC program and citing Scranton's pending BRIC buyout funding, but there is no record of him co-sponsoring a specific bill called the 'Save BRIC Act.' This appears to be an invented or misattributed piece of legislation.

inaccurate_statement: Reformed WRDA guidelines to mandate that flood feasibility studies be reviewed concurrently across USACE levels rather than sequentially, slicing project timelines
description: No record supports this specific claim about mandating concurrent (rather than sequential) USACE review levels. His documented WRDA work involves expanding Section 566 eligibility to the Upper Delaware River Basin and raising program authorization funding levels, not this specific procedural reform.

inaccurate_statement: Submitted millions in FY 2027 appropriations requests, including $1.7 million for Honesdale Borough stormwater management and over $2.2 million for municipal wastewater expansions in Dallas Area, Milford, and Westfall
description: Bresnahan is documented as having secured similar-sounding but different, specific figures for wastewater/stormwater projects (e.g., $1.25M Monroe County, $1M Dallas Area Municipal Authority, $8M Exeter sewer/stormwater project). The specific figures and locations cited here (Honesdale Borough $1.7 million; Milford and Westfall $2.2 million) do not match any documented funding requests and appear to be fabricated or invented details.

inaccurate_statement: Secure America Act provides long-term funding through September 2029 for CBP and ICE
description: The Secure America Act is confirmed as legislation Bresnahan voted for that provides long-term ICE/CBP funding, but the specific end date of 'September 2029' is not confirmed by available records, which describe the funding as long-term without specifying that exact date.

inaccurate_statement: He supported major legislative packages, including a $46.5 billion investment to complete construction on the southern border wall
description: The knowledge base confirms Bresnahan voted for the Secure America Act, which provides long-term ICE/CBP funding, and that he supports completing the border wall generally, but no specific $46.5 billion wall-construction figure tied to his vote is documented in the available material. This specific dollar figure appears to be an unverified or invented elaboration rather than a confirmed legislative detail.

inaccurate_statement: Bresnahan often contrasts his career as a real estate developer and venture capitalist with career politicians.
description: Bresnahan's documented professional background is as CEO of Kuharchik Construction, an electrical contracting business, and as founder of RPB Ventures, a real estate development firm — there is no record of him working as a venture capitalist. inaccurate_statement: Perry recently collaborated directly with the U.S. Department of Transportation to navigate the review process and advance the timeline for the I-83 South Bridge replacement project
description: Perry's documented I-83 South Bridge advocacy consists of a 2024 joint congressional delegation letter to then-Secretary Buttigieg urging discretionary funding; no record exists of a more recent direct collaboration specifically advancing DOT's review timeline as described here.

description: No record of this specific statement or position exists in Perry's documented platform, voting record, or public statements. His House.gov and campaign site issues pages have no public-safety/crime section, and no comparable statement about the Insurrection Act was found.

description: No record of Perry signing a 'Heritage Action Police Pledge' appears in his documented record, which lists no dedicated public-safety plank at all.

description: No record of this specific amendment concerning license plate readers exists in Perry's documented legislative record.

description: No record of this legislation or characterization appears in Perry's documented record.
