description: Perry does have a well-documented immigration/border-security platform, but this specific framing tying it explicitly to 'public safety' as a category is not directly supported; his documented public-safety plank is confirmed to not exist as a dedicated platform item.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supports H.R. 2 (the Secure America's Borders Act) as a primary legislative solution
description: H.R. 2 in the 118th Congress, which Perry voted for, was titled the Secure the Border Act of 2023, not the "Secure America's Borders Act." There is a similarly named 2025-cycle bill ("Secure America's Borders Act" or related "Permanent Trump Secure Border Act") in Perry's record, but the specific naming here conflates or garbles the bill title; his confirmed vote was for the Secure the Border Act (H.R. 2, 2023).

inaccurate_statement: Perry opposes sending U.S. taxpayer funds to other countries for foreign aid or border security abroad until the domestic border crisis is resolved
description: No record supports a blanket policy of halting all foreign aid until the border is secured; available material shows Perry's border stance centers on enforcement metrics, barriers, and staffing, not a specific foreign-aid-conditionality demand framed this way. This appears to be an unsupported extrapolation rather than a documented position.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson advocates for making child tax credits permanent
description: No record exists of Stelson making a specific pledge to make the child tax credit permanent. Her documented platform focuses on affordability generally (tariffs, gas, housing, prescription drugs), middle-class tax relief, and other specific proposals, but a specific child-tax-credit permanence pledge is not among her confirmed, sourced positions.

inaccurate_statement: Perry prioritizes traditional conservative family values
description: There is no documented statement from Perry framing his platform explicitly around 'traditional conservative family values' as a stated plank; his confirmed platform centers on deregulation, reduced spending, border security, and an all-of-the-above energy strategy. This is an unsupported characterization not tied to any specific sourced statement.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson focuses heavily on curbing gun violence through targeted legislative measures, such as mandating the reporting of lost or stolen firearms
description: No documentation of Stelson specifically proposing a mandatory lost-or-stolen-firearm reporting requirement was found. Her documented gun-safety platform (via GIFFORDS) covers expanding background checks, red flag laws, safe storage incentives, addressing ghost guns, and community violence intervention funding, but a specific 'reporting lost or stolen firearms' mandate is not among the confirmed planks and appears to be an invented specific detail layered onto an otherwise accurate general position.

inaccurate_statement: Perry promotes the Stop Insider Trading Act at the federal level
description: No record exists of Scott Perry sponsoring or promoting a 'Stop Insider Trading Act.' Perry's actual congressional stock-trading-related legislative activity documented is that he has sponsored legislation to prohibit members of Congress from trading individual stocks — a different, though related, measure. Attributing a specifically named 'Stop Insider Trading Act' to him is not supported and appears fabricated. This is a narrow supporting detail that doesn't change the response's overall characterization of Perry's crime platform.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's position 'isn't simply more gun restrictions'; framed instead around accountability/prevention with mandatory uniforms/badges rather than her documented gun-restriction platform
description: Stelson's documented public-safety-adjacent platform centers on expanding gun-violence-prevention measures (expanded background checks, red flag laws, safe storage incentives, targeting ghost guns, domestic-abuser firearm restrictions) per her GIFFORDS endorsement profile, not a generic 'accountability plus prevention' framing that omits this. The response's description of her public-safety approach omits her actual documented gun-policy platform, giving an incomplete picture, though it doesn't invert her overall stance.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supports increasing federal mandatory minimum sentencing guidelines as a deterrent against repeat and violent offenders
description: No direct statement or documented platform item was found showing Perry has taken a specific position advocating stricter federal mandatory sentencing guidelines. His documented public-safety-adjacent record centers on opposing new gun restrictions and supporting law-enforcement-related legislation, with no dedicated current sentencing-policy plank identified.

inaccurate_statement: Perry frequently advocates for federal measures targeting drug trafficking—particularly fentanyl—and supports more rigid sentencing laws for violent crimes.
description: No record exists of a specific, current fentanyl-trafficking or violent-crime-sentencing platform plank for Perry. His documented public-safety-adjacent positions are limited to immigration enforcement, Second Amendment views, and general law-enforcement support language; no dedicated fentanyl or sentencing-law statement was found despite repeated dedicated searches for a public-safety plank.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has consistently opposed several federal police reform proposals that he argues limit qualified immunity or overly restrict law enforcement procedures.
description: No documented voting record or statement ties Perry specifically to opposing qualified-immunity reform bills. His public-safety record as documented consists of votes on immigration enforcement and general pro-law-enforcement statements; no specific qualified-immunity-related legislative opposition was found.

inaccurate_statement: Janelle Stelson publicly opposes local ICE raids that disrupt community safety and cause fear
description: Stelson's actual platform does not state opposition to ICE raids themselves. Her campaign site says she opposes open borders and supports deportation of violent criminals, while calling for accountability measures such as independent investigations of ICE incidents/killings, ICE agents wearing uniforms/badges instead of masks, and due process protections. This is a reform/accountability position, not a blanket opposition to 'local ICE raids that disrupt community safety and cause fear.' The claim overstates and mischaracterizes her stance as anti-enforcement, when analysts describe her as supporting stronger border security and tougher enforcement with due-process caveats. This is a narrower framing issue rather than a fabricated fact, so it's misleading but not a wholesale invention.

inaccurate_statement: Janelle Stelson advocates for reforming labor laws to support the district's agricultural workforce
description: Stelson has published a detailed rural/agriculture policy platform (Farm Bill renewal, right-to-repair equipment, poultry/Big Ag consolidation, tariffs, avian flu response, rural broadband, rural healthcare) and a separate labor platform (raising the minimum wage, strengthening union organizing rights, vocational training), but neither her campaign site's priorities page, her rural policy PDF, nor other sourcing found any statement specifically advocating for 'reforming labor laws to support the district's agricultural workforce' (e.g., farmworker wage/labor protections, H-2A visa reform, or farm labor organizing). Her labor positions are framed generally for all workers, and her agriculture positions focus on farm economics/equipment rather than farm labor law. The claim appears to conflate her general labor stance with her separate farm-economy platform, and this specific combined claim is not substantiated by available sources. This is a narrow, specific policy claim that doesn't undermine the broader accurate point that she supports both farmers and labor generally, so it is best characterized as a minor fabrication rather than one that would change the overall takeaway.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson supports expanding Medicaid and community health centers
description: No record exists of Stelson making a specific platform statement about expanding community health centers; her documented healthcare platform focuses on affordable care access, ending surprise billing, extending ACA subsidies, and expanding Medicare drug-price negotiation, along with opposing Medicaid cuts, but a specific 'community health centers' expansion pledge is not found in her documented positions.

inaccurate_statement: Perry voted against the Affordable Care Act
description: Scott Perry was first elected to Congress in 2012 and took office in January 2013; the Affordable Care Act was passed and signed into law in March 2010, before he was in Congress, so he could not have cast a vote on it. His documented record includes opposing and voting to repeal/undermine the ACA in various ways since taking office, but he never voted against its original passage.

inaccurate_statement: Janelle Stelson seeks a permanent child tax credit and a higher minimum wage
description: No record exists of Stelson proposing a permanent child tax credit or a higher federal minimum wage as part of her platform. Her documented affordability platform focuses on tariffs, healthcare costs, small-business support, and middle-class tax relief, without a specific child tax credit or minimum wage proposal on record.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry favors reducing federal spending on the Affordable Care Act to limit government debt as his 'free-market healthcare' approach
description: Perry's documented healthcare position centers on market-oriented alternatives like small-business insurance pooling and opposition to expanded federal subsidies, along with support for the 2025 reconciliation bill's Medicaid work requirements, rather than a stated goal of cutting ACA spending specifically to reduce the debt.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson supports robust alliances, international coalitions, and strategic foreign assistance to counter global threats, and is supportive of working with international allies to curb hostile actions abroad.
description: Available reporting indicates Stelson has taken more hawkish positions than this characterization suggests — she has said she supports Israel's right to 'root out Hamas and decimate the terrorist organization' and has called for continued aid to Ukraine, with some commentary describing her Ukraine stance as notably hawkish. The response's framing of her as favoring measured multilateral stability-building is a plausible but incomplete gloss that doesn't fully capture the more assertive tenor of her actual public statements on Israel and Ukraine.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson opposes the hardline tactics of the previous Trump administration on the border, citing humanitarian concerns.
description: Stelson's documented immigration statements emphasize opposing 'open borders,' focusing deportations on violent criminals, requiring ICE to be identifiable and follow due process, and increasing border technology and staffing — a specific, detailed platform. No direct statement was found explicitly framing her position as rejecting 'hardline tactics... citing humanitarian concerns' in those terms; this is a plausible but unverified gloss on her platform rather than a documented quote or position.

inaccurate_statement: Perry served nearly 40 years in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard
description: Perry's National Guard service ran from 1980 to 2019, which is approximately 39 years — this is essentially accurate and close enough to 'nearly 40 years' to not be a meaningful error; however, noting for completeness that the figure is a rounding of the documented 1980–2019 span.

inaccurate_statement: Perry leans heavily toward non-interventionism and opposes open-ended foreign aid or military engagements without distinct, immediate U.S. security outcomes.
description: The available record shows Perry supported the Trump administration's 2026 military action against Iran and voted against a House resolution that would have required removing U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran — actions inconsistent with a strongly non-interventionist characterization. While Freedom Caucus members are often skeptical of unconditional foreign aid, presenting Perry as leaning heavily non-interventionist without noting his support for the Iran strikes gives an incomplete and somewhat misleading picture of his actual foreign-policy record.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson is running with the endorsement of the Pennsylvania AFL-CIO
description: There is no record of a Pennsylvania AFL-CIO endorsement of Stelson in the available material. Her documented labor endorsements include AFGE Local 2004, United Brotherhood of Carpenters and Joiners, PA Professional Fire Fighters Association, United Mine Workers of America, IBEW Local 229, PA Building & Construction Trades Council, National Education Association, United Steelworkers District 10, and PA Conference of Teamsters, but not a specific Pennsylvania AFL-CIO endorsement. A specific research pass on Stelson's endorsements found several fabricated union-endorsement claims for unrelated unions, suggesting this may be another instance of an invented labor endorsement rather than one simply missed by that research.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson has an endorsement from the PA AFL-CIO
description: No record of a PA AFL-CIO endorsement of Stelson appears in her documented endorsement list, which includes a large slate of specific unions (AFGE Local 2004, United Brotherhood of Carpenters, PA Professional Fire Fighters, United Mine Workers, IBEW Local 229, PA Building & Construction Trades Council, NEA, United Steelworkers District 10, PA Conference of Teamsters, and others) but does not include the PA AFL-CIO by name. Given the documented pattern of fabricated or misattributed union endorsements for this candidate in other checks, this specific claim cannot be confirmed and is treated as unsupported. This is a narrow endorsement detail that does not undermine the broader accurate point that she has extensive labor support.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson is endorsed by the PA AFL-CIO and champions union protections, fair pay, and worker-centric policies
description: No record of a specific 'PA AFL-CIO' endorsement of Stelson was found; her documented labor endorsements include AFGE Local 2004, United Brotherhood of Carpenters and Joiners, PA Professional Fire Fighters Association, United Mine Workers of America, IBEW Local 229, PA Building & Construction Trades Council, National Education Association, United Steelworkers District 10, and PA Conference of Teamsters, but not a specifically named PA AFL-CIO endorsement. Her general support for union protections and fair pay is well documented and accurate, so only the specific named endorser is unverified/unsupported.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry argues manufacturing jobs are best protected via deregulation and tax cuts to keep factories competitive (implying this is his full stated approach)
description: While generally consistent with Perry's deregulation/tax-cut framing, his platform and record also include specific, targeted manufacturing interventions the response omits, such as his direct July 2025 letter urging Cleveland-Cliffs to reopen the Steelton steel mill and his push for tariff exemptions on cocoa imports to protect Pennsylvania chocolate manufacturers, meaning his manufacturing approach isn't purely hands-off free-market as implied.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson has prioritized infrastructure readiness, framing flash flooding from torrential storms as a critical issue threatening 25% of local infrastructure.
description: No statement from Stelson framing flash flooding as threatening '25% of local infrastructure' exists in her documented platform; her flood-management position is a confirmed research gap with no direct statement found on this topic at all, making this specific statistic and framing unsupported.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's platform centers on using federal funding to update aging infrastructure—such as flood walls, levees, and stream restoration—to handle shifting weather patterns.
description: Stelson has made general statements supporting infrastructure investment in roads, bridges, public transit and the electric grid, but no specific statement mentioning flood walls, levees, or stream restoration has been found; flood management is a confirmed gap in her documented platform.

inaccurate_statement: Perry voted against certain federal flood insurance reform measures to minimize federal spending.
description: Available voting records point the other way on the specific flood insurance votes identifiable. Club for Growth's scorecard shows that on SB1182, which extended the National Flood Insurance Program, Perry's actual vote was 'Y' (yes/for), even though the fiscally conservative group wanted a 'no' vote, faulting the extension as 'fiscally irresponsible.' Separately, in a 2014 statement, Perry expressed support for H.R. 3370, which rolled back some Biggert-Waters NFIP reforms to protect homeowners' property values, while noting he would have preferred deeper structural/fiscal reforms but voted for the bill anyway. No identifiable instance was found of Perry voting against an NFIP/flood insurance reform bill specifically citing federal spending minimization as the reason. The claim's core framing (Perry as an opponent of flood insurance measures on fiscal grounds) is not well supported by the specific votes found; it may be a generic inference from his general fiscal-conservative reputation rather than a documented fact tied to actual flood insurance votes, so it's rated a minor inaccuracy rather than a fully fabricated one given the lack of exhaustive certainty.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson advocates for upgrading regional infrastructure to address climate-driven flash floods, frequently citing her decades as a local news anchor witnessing increased flash flooding as a key motivator for updating local drainage and levee infrastructure
description: No direct statement on flood management from Stelson was found after dedicated research, including a specific re-check against 2026 flood-management coverage. This response invents a detailed, specific flood-mitigation platform (drainage/levee upgrades, anchor-career motivation) that has no documented basis and directly answers the user's specific question with fabricated specificity.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has argued against FEMA pre-positioning assets for localized flood warnings, stating that it is unfeasible for the agency to anticipate every regional fast-moving disaster, favoring fiscal restraint and deregulation over federally funded climate adaptation plans
description: No flood-management statement from Perry was found after a dedicated search of his House.gov issues pages, campaign site, and local news. This specific claim about his stated FEMA philosophy and rhetoric is not documented and appears fabricated to directly answer the user's flood-specific question.

description: This specific vote is not documented in the available material and could not be verified; given the response fabricates other flood-related specifics about Perry as well, this claim is treated as unsupported.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson advocates for integrating climate-resiliency standards into local development so that roads, bridges, and culverts are engineered to withstand modern, high-volume flooding events.
description: No direct statement or campaign material was found showing Stelson has proposed integrating climate-resiliency engineering standards for roads, bridges, and culverts. Her documented platform on infrastructure emphasizes general investment in roads, bridges, public transportation, and the electric grid as job creators, but no source ties this to flood-resiliency engineering standards specifically; flood management is a confirmed, dedicated research gap for her.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson supports using federal funds to repair local dams and reinforce vulnerable flood walls across South-Central Pennsylvania.
description: No statement from Stelson naming dam repair or flood-wall reinforcement as a platform item was found. Flood management is explicitly documented as a confirmed gap with no direct statement found from her on this topic despite dedicated searches.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson emphasizes keeping federal safety nets and emergency management agencies fully funded and accessible to ensure rapid financial support and infrastructure recovery after major storm events.
description: No sourced statement ties Stelson to a specific disaster-relief/emergency-management funding position. Her documented platform covers affordability, healthcare, immigration, and jobs, but no material addresses FEMA funding or disaster recovery specifically.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson generally aligns with mainstream Democratic priorities that support maximizing federal dollars for local projects, including utilizing Bipartisan Infrastructure Law funds to upgrade aging stormwater systems.
description: While Stelson has praised the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act generally for its Pennsylvania road/bridge investments and job creation, no source shows her specifically proposing stormwater-system upgrades under that law. This is an invented specific policy mechanism attributed to her without support.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson advocates for direct federal resources to local police departments for training, staffing, and transparency
description: No source documents Stelson proposing direct federal funding to local police departments specifically for training, staffing, and transparency; her documented public-safety-adjacent platform centers on gun-violence-prevention measures (background checks, red flag laws, safe storage, community violence intervention programs) rather than a police-funding/staffing proposal.

inaccurate_statement: Perry votes for stringent sentencing measures and opposes federal overreach in local policing
description: No documented current, dedicated public-safety/sentencing plank or specific sentencing votes exist in the available record for Perry; his platform's public-safety-adjacent content is centered on immigration enforcement and Second Amendment issues, not a documented record of 'stringent sentencing' votes or an explicit anti-federal-overreach-in-local-policing position. This is an unsupported specific characterization of his legislative record.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry signed the 'Police Pledge' to oppose defunding law enforcement
description: No record of Perry signing a 'Police Pledge' exists in his documented record. His public-safety positioning is limited to general statements and specific votes (e.g., a D.C. police-budget amendment); this specific named pledge is not substantiated.

inaccurate_statement: Perry filed a legislative amendment to prevent Washington, D.C. from reducing its police department's budget
description: No documentation supports Perry introducing an amendment specifically targeting Washington, D.C.'s police budget. His known public-safety-adjacent record includes general law-enforcement-supportive votes and a 2017 Fairness for Crime Victims Act, but no D.C.-budget amendment is documented.

inaccurate_statement: Perry voted to increase ICE funding by $75 billion
description: No record supports this specific $75 billion ICE funding figure being tied to a Perry vote. His documented immigration-enforcement record includes cosponsoring several enforcement-focused bills, but this specific number and vote are not corroborated.

inaccurate_statement: Perry voted for budget packages that included cuts to the Community Oriented Policing Services (COPS) grant program
description: No documented vote or budget proposal tying Perry specifically to COPS program cuts was found in his record. This appears to be an invented specific claim not grounded in his documented voting history.

inaccurate_statement: Perry does not participate in the congressional earmark process and does not request federal earmarks for local community projects
description: No documentation in Perry's record addresses his earmark-request practices one way or another; this specific claim about his earmark behavior is unsubstantiated and appears fabricated.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has explicitly stated that calling to defund the police invites community violence
description: No specific quote or statement matching this exact framing is documented in Perry's record. While he is broadly understood to oppose defunding the police, this precise claim/quote is unsubstantiated.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson supports reinforcing federal COPS grant programs to help local departments hire officers
description: No documented statement from Stelson specifically endorses the federal COPS grant program. Her public-safety-related platform items documented are broader (gun-violence prevention measures, community violence intervention funding), not a specific COPS-program endorsement.

inaccurate_statement: Perry signed the Heritage Action Police Pledge, formally committing to oppose any measures to 'Defund the Police'
description: No record of Perry signing a 'Heritage Action Police Pledge' appears in his documented public-safety record, which notes no dedicated current public-safety/crime platform plank exists and only an unconfirmed tweet referencing support for law enforcement. This specific pledge claim is not supported by any available source.

inaccurate_statement: Perry voted for proposals like the Default on America Act, which sought cuts to federal law enforcement budgets including COPS grants
description: There is no record of Perry voting for a bill called the 'Default on America Act' or of specific cuts to COPS grants tied to him in his documented record. This claim is unsupported by the available material on his legislative record.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's platform is 'around clean energy investments and stronger accountability for large industrial energy users' as the specific framing of her data center opposition
description: Stelson's confirmed direct statement on data centers focuses on the impact on neighborhoods, family homes/farms, and support for letting local governments say no to projects until resident concerns on water/grid/noise are addressed - not specifically a framing around 'clean energy investments and stronger accountability for large industrial energy users,' which is a different emphasis not documented in her platform on this topic.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's stance is described as strongly supporting accelerating AI and data center infrastructure with no mention of his stated view that data-center zoning/regulation is a local-municipality matter outside his federal purview
description: Perry has publicly stated that data-center siting and zoning are local decisions outside his role as "a federal guy," saying he doesn't get into local zoning and building decisions municipalities make. The response omits this and instead frames him solely as an aggressive pro-buildout advocate based on his national comments about not slowing down AI competition with China, which gives an incomplete picture of his documented position on this specific topic.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson has voiced support for tighter administrative guardrails and state-level actions to hold large tech infrastructure accountable
description: The documented record shows Stelson made general remarks to CNBC about data centers encroaching on neighborhoods and supporting a federal role letting local governments say no to projects, but no source describes her advocating specifically for 'state-level actions' or 'tighter administrative guardrails' as a distinct policy mechanism. This adds specificity beyond what is documented, though it is broadly consistent with her general sympathetic stance on the issue.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's past legislative votes and public statements lean toward supporting fast-tracked technological growth rather than placing restrictions or moratoriums on the industry
description: While Perry has made a national-level comment that the U.S. 'can't afford to slow down the build-out' of data centers, his specific documented statement on data-center siting is that he considers it a local zoning matter outside federal purview -- he has not been shown to have taken legislative votes specifically fast-tracking data-center construction or opposing moratoriums. The response overstates the specificity and legislative basis of this position.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson vows to repeal tariffs on construction materials/lumber to bring down homebuilding costs
description: Stelson's platform calls for repealing broad tariffs generally (blaming them for raising costs on food, gas, housing, and more) and criticizes Perry's tariff policy, but no specific statement singling out lumber/building-material tariffs as a distinct housing-cost policy was found in her documented platform.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson supports making the Child Tax Credit permanent and expanding tax credit programs like the Child Tax Credit
description: Stelson's documented platform includes middle-class tax relief generally, but no direct statement specifically calling for making the Child Tax Credit permanent was found in her platform materials.

inaccurate_statement: Perry was the only member of Pennsylvania's congressional delegation to vote against the bipartisan housing bill.
description: The housing bill (21st Century ROAD to Housing Act) passed the House 396-13 (or 358-32, per other sourcing), with Perry among a small group of dissenting Republicans nationally. The knowledge base confirms Perry was the only Pennsylvania representative to vote against it, which supports this specific framing as accurate rather than inaccurate — however, the vote count details elsewhere vary (396-13 vs 358-32) across records, indicating some inconsistency in the underlying figures reported for this bill across sources, though the core claim about Perry being the lone PA dissenter is supported.

inaccurate_statement: Perry suggests placing data centers near local power sources to supply surplus energy back to the grid and lower long-term consumer costs
description: Search results show no evidence Scott Perry (PA-10) proposed placing data centers near local power sources to feed surplus energy back to the grid. A CNBC report directly quotes Perry saying that while he's engaged on national energy policy, he largely views data center regulation as out of his purview -- essentially the opposite of proactively proposing a specific data-center siting/grid policy. The specific idea described in the claim (data centers near power sources supplying surplus energy back to the grid) closely tracks proposals discussed in coverage of Virginia state Senator Russet Perry (a Democrat from Loudoun County), a completely different 'Perry,' suggesting the claim conflates or misattributes someone else's proposal to Scott Perry. No campaign materials, press releases, or interviews from Scott Perry surfaced supporting this claim, and his one substantive on-record comment on data centers explicitly disclaims taking such a policy stance.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry opposed caps on Medicare out-of-pocket costs
description: Perry actually backed H.R. 19, the Lower Costs, More Cures Act of 2019, which included a first-ever Part D out-of-pocket cost cap and capped insulin costs at $50/month. There is no record of him opposing Medicare out-of-pocket cost caps; if anything the documented record shows the opposite on this specific provision.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry voted against capping out-of-pocket costs for Medicare
description: Available records indicate Perry actually backed 2019-era Republican legislation (H.R. 19, the Lower Costs, More Cures Act) that included a first-ever Part D out-of-pocket cost cap and a $50/month insulin cap, rather than voting against capping such costs. This contradicts the claim that he opposed an out-of-pocket cap, though it's a narrow point about a specific historical vote rather than his overall healthcare stance.

inaccurate_statement: Perry advocates for redirecting existing, unused federal funds to cover transportation bonds rather than introducing new taxes or major federal spending packages
description: No record exists of Perry proposing a specific mechanism of redirecting unused federal funds to cover transportation bonds. His documented infrastructure positions focus on deregulation, speeding environmental review/permitting, and specific advocacy for the I-83 South Bridge replacement funding, not this specific bonds mechanism.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry's public safety platform includes introducing and backing federal measures to target global criminal organizations and malign foreign activities, framed as part of a dedicated public-safety/crime plan
description: Perry's documented platform has no dedicated public-safety or crime section on either his House.gov issues page or his campaign site; his current issue categories are Agriculture, Defense and National Security, Economy and Jobs, Education, Energy, Federal Spending, Health Care, Immigration, Right to Life, Second Amendment, Social Security and Medicare, Transportation, and Veterans Issues. Any content about targeting international criminal networks would fall under Defense and National Security (terrorism/homeland-security framed) rather than a distinct crime-reduction plan, and this framing overstates the specificity of his platform on local crime.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry's public safety focus includes eliminating waste, fraud, and abuse in federal operations to strengthen public safety and fiscal accountability, presented as part of his crime-reduction platform
description: There is no documented statement tying Perry's federal spending/anti-waste positions specifically to a crime-reduction or public-safety plan; his federal-spending platform is about fiscal policy generally, not local crime reduction, and no dedicated public-safety plank exists in his platform materials.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson supports expanding an 'all-of-the-above' energy strategy that heavily incorporates wind and solar power.
description: The 'all-of-the-above' energy strategy label specifically describes Scott Perry's platform (which includes hydropower, oil, and gas), not Stelson's. Stelson's documented position is support for expanding clean-energy investment and incentives generally, with no specific statement naming wind and solar or using the 'all-of-the-above' framing. Attributing Perry's specific strategy label to Stelson misrepresents her platform, though the general point that she supports clean energy is directionally accurate.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's plan includes 'Targeted Investments: Championing affordable housing initiatives to create local construction jobs and attract new workers to Central Pennsylvania'
description: Stelson does support federal investment in affordable housing as part of her affordability platform, but no source ties this specifically to a stated goal of creating local construction jobs or attracting new workers to the region — that specific framing/mechanism is not documented in her platform materials.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's 'Workforce Stability' pillar expands access to affordable healthcare specifically framed as improving worker retention
description: Stelson does support affordable healthcare access as a general platform priority, but no source frames this specifically as a worker-retention/workforce-stability jobs strategy — this appears to be an invented connection between two separate, real planks of her platform.

inaccurate_statement: Describes Scott Perry as 'Incumbent' and Janelle Stelson as 'Challenger' without noting this is a rematch of their 2024 race
description: While technically accurate that Perry is the incumbent and Stelson the challenger, the response omits that this is a rematch from the November 2024 election, where Perry narrowly defeated Stelson by about 1.2 points. This is a framing omission rather than a direct factual error, since the labels themselves are correct, but it fails to convey important context about the race's history.

inaccurate_statement: Describes Scott Perry as 'Incumbent' and Janelle Stelson as 'Challenger' without noting this is a rematch of their 2024 race
description: While technically accurate that Perry is the incumbent and Stelson the challenger, the response omits that this is a rematch from the November 2024 election, where Perry narrowly defeated Stelson by about 1.2 points. This is a framing omission rather than a direct factual error, since the labels themselves are correct, but it fails to convey important context about the race's history.

inaccurate_statement: Perry argues that lowering fuel costs is the most efficient way to relieve economic pressure on commuters, implying this is his primary transportation/commute-fixing strategy
description: Perry's documented positions on gas prices focus on ending the Iran war and returning to pre-war energy price levels, and are framed as part of general affordability messaging rather than specifically as his strategy for fixing commutes or traffic congestion. His actual infrastructure-specific record is centered on advocacy for the I-83 South Bridge project and skepticism of transit spending, not fuel-price arguments, so conflating the two overstates and mischaracterizes his stated approach to commute/traffic problems specifically.

inaccurate_statement: Voters are weighing 'strict anti-abortion positions held by Scott Perry' against Stelson's platform.
description: Scott Perry's abortion record is genuinely conflicting rather than simply 'strict anti-abortion': his campaign materials state he supports exceptions for rape, incest, and life of the mother, and he co-introduced the IVF Protection Act to support IVF access, while he also currently cosponsors the Life at Conception Act, which contains no such exceptions and defines personhood from the moment of fertilization. Characterizing his position as simply 'strict anti-abortion' without acknowledging his stated exceptions and IVF support presents only one side of a documented, conflicting record.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has focused legislative efforts on combating the opioid epidemic and looking for ways to streamline federal resources for local communities
description: No record in Perry's documented legislative history or platform materials specifically identifies combating the opioid epidemic as a focal legislative effort; his healthcare record centers on ACA repeal-era messaging, the 2025 reconciliation bill, Medicaid work requirements, and prescription drug cost positions, not opioid-epidemic-specific initiatives. This is a narrow, unverified addition to his healthcare record rather than a claim that changes the overall picture of his platform.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's safety platform is endorsed by prominent labor organizations like the Transport Workers Union (TWU).
description: The specific claim that the Transport Workers Union endorsed Stelson traces to an endorsement roster that actually belongs to a different candidate (Sharif Street in PA-3), not to Stelson's real, documented union endorsement list, which includes groups like AFGE, the Pennsylvania Conference of Teamsters, and the United Mine Workers of America but not TWU.

inaccurate_statement: Perry secured a $500 million grant to replace the I-83 South Bridge
description: The I-83 South Bridge replacement is projected to cost $1.1–1.3 billion, and the documented record shows Perry co-signed a 2024 letter with Pennsylvania's congressional delegation urging federal discretionary funding for the project — there is no confirmed $500 million grant secured specifically through his efforts. The specific dollar figure and framing as a grant he personally secured is not supported.

inaccurate_statement: Perry recently hosted U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy in the district to advocate for the regional construction and trucking workforce
description: No record exists of Perry hosting Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy in PA-10. The documented 2026 meeting involving Perry on highway/infrastructure matters was with local trucking/construction stakeholders and federal transportation officials in Cumberland County, not a visit specifically framed as hosting the sitting Transportation Secretary.

inaccurate_statement: Perry voted against the $1 trillion national infrastructure bill, citing concerns over inflation, national debt, and tied-in green energy mandates
description: Perry did vote against the 2021 bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, but no documented statement ties his opposition specifically to 'green energy mandates' as a stated reason; his documented rationale centers on spending, debt, and inflation concerns generally rather than this specific framing.

inaccurate_statement: Central Pennsylvania deserves its fair share of the $11.3 billion allocated for state roads and $1.6 billion for bridge repairs (attributed to Stelson's stated argument)
description: No source in the available material documents Stelson citing these specific dollar figures ($11.3 billion for state roads, $1.6 billion for bridge repairs) in relation to the IIJA or PA-10. Her confirmed infrastructure statements emphasize investment in roads, bridges, public transportation, and the electric grid generally, and highlighting the I-83 South Bridge specifically, but this specific pair of numbers is not documented anywhere in her platform materials.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson advocates for repealing specific tariffs on building materials like lumber and drywall, arguing they inflate the cost of physical infrastructure and housing projects
description: Stelson's documented tariff criticism centers on general cost-of-living tariffs affecting food, gas, and household goods, and specifically construction-adjacent tariffs on affordability broadly, but no record exists of her naming lumber or drywall specifically as targets for tariff repeal tied to infrastructure/housing cost inflation.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson released a targeted supplemental housing plan aimed at expanding small-dollar home loans for first-time buyers and prioritizing Federal Housing Administration (FHA) mortgage guarantees.
description: No record exists of Stelson releasing a specific housing plan detailing small-dollar home loans or FHA mortgage guarantee prioritization. Her documented platform supports federal investment in affordable housing broadly, but this specific policy mechanism with these particular details is not substantiated and appears to be a fabricated specific plan.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson advocates for repealing certain tariffs on construction materials like drywall and lumber, arguing these supply-side restrictions directly inflate building costs and home prices.
description: Stelson's documented platform opposes broad tariffs generally and blames tariffs for raising costs of goods including housing, but no specific statement naming drywall or lumber tariffs specifically was found. This appears to be an invented level of specificity not grounded in her actual documented statements.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson proposes addressing high mortgage interest rates by curbing federal deficit spending, though specific spending cuts have not been detailed.
description: No record exists of Stelson framing mortgage interest rates as a target of deficit-spending curbs. Her documented affordability platform focuses on tariffs, healthcare costs, and targeted tax relief rather than deficit reduction as a mortgage-rate strategy; this specific claim appears fabricated.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's plan calls for repealing building material tariffs and expanding FHA-backed programs and small-dollar loans to address housing costs.
description: No record in her documented platform mentions FHA-backed programs, small-dollar loans, or a specific building-material-tariff repeal; her housing platform is limited to general federal investment in affordable housing and increasing housing supply, without this level of specific mechanism detail being confirmed.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's healthcare and utilities plan includes capping 'junk fees.'
description: No documented statement shows Stelson using 'junk fees' capping as part of her healthcare/utilities platform; her documented healthcare positions focus on ACA subsidies, drug pricing negotiation, surprise billing, and medical debt, not a junk-fee cap framed this way.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's opposition to the housing bill was rooted in preventing federal overreach, specifically citing concerns over provisions linked to a central bank digital currency.
description: No record supports Perry citing a central bank digital currency provision as his reason for opposing the housing bill. His documented rationale for opposing tariff-related and spending bills centers on federal spending, regulatory overreach, and specific policy objections, but no source ties his housing-bill vote to CBDC concerns; this appears to be a fabricated specific rationale.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson advocates for increasing minimum wage standards and addressing corporate price gouging to ease the financial burden at the pump as part of her gas-price strategy.
description: Stelson's gas-price commentary specifically blames tariffs and the Iran war and calls for repealing tariffs and more stable foreign policy; her platform's minimum-wage plank is tied to jobs/wages, not gas prices specifically, and no platform statement or news coverage ties a 'corporate price gouging' policy to her gas-price plan. Reporting has specifically noted she offered relatively few concrete policy solutions on gas prices, making this attribution of specific additional mechanisms to her gas-price strategy unsupported and misleading.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry opposes government price-setting mechanisms and favors free-market approaches to healthcare (presented as his complete/only position without noting nuance)
description: Perry's documented positions on prescription drugs include both opposition to Medicare drug-price negotiation (voting against H.R.3 and cosponsoring repeal of IRA negotiation authority) and market-oriented rhetoric about Big Pharma providing cures, which broadly supports this characterization as a general framing. This is not contradicted by the available record, though it simplifies a more detailed record of specific votes and cosponsorships.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry is a member of the House Homeland Security Committee
description: Scott Perry's current (119th Congress) committee assignments are House Oversight and Government Reform, Transportation and Infrastructure, the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, and Foreign Affairs. He is not documented as a member of the House Homeland Security Committee.

inaccurate_statement: A federal judge ultimately ordered him to turn over more than 2,000 records to the Department of Justice
description: The dispute over Perry's seized phone records was litigated up through the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals (an appellate court), not resolved by a single federal district judge's order; the appellate ruling permitted access to 1,659 of the roughly 2,219 contested messages by December 2023, not simply 'more than 2,000 records' turned over as ordered by 'a federal judge.'

inaccurate_statement: Stelson made the cat café remark during her 2024 primary run and it was an old, decades-old broadcast segment unearthed by opponents then.
description: The remark was a real, pre-candidacy on-air comment from Stelson's broadcast journalism career, but it is documented as resurfacing as a 2024 campaign issue generally, not specifically characterized as being unearthed during her 2024 primary run as a decades-old clip in the way described. The location was also described as Belgium generally (a Belgian cat café), not specifically 'Brussels' as stated. This is a narrow, non-central detail that doesn't change the core accurate point that the remark is real and was a 2024 campaign controversy.

inaccurate_statement: A federal judge ordered Perry to hand over the records after the legal battle over Speech or Debate Clause protections.
description: The actual resolution was a D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals ruling (an appellate court decision), which permitted investigators access to the large majority of the contested messages (1,659 of 2,219 documents by December 2023) — not a single federal district judge's order framed as simply commanding him to "hand over the records." This is a narrow procedural mischaracterization rather than a fundamental misstatement of the outcome, since access was indeed ultimately granted to investigators.

inaccurate_statement: Janelle Stelson has a 30-year background as a local TV news anchor
description: Stelson's broadcast journalism career spanned nearly 40 years overall, with 26 years specifically as an anchor at WGAL-TV Lancaster — neither figure matches the stated '30-year' framing.

inaccurate_statement: Janelle Stelson emphasizes her 30-year career as a local TV news anchor
description: Stelson had a nearly 40-year broadcast journalism career overall, and specifically spent 26 years (1997-2023) as an anchor at WGAL-TV Lancaster, not 30 years as a local news anchor.

inaccurate_statement: Janelle Stelson has accepted corporate PAC money to build her campaign war chest
description: Stelson's campaign finance breakdown shows PAC/other-committee contributions are about 8% of her total receipts, and multiple entries in the accuracy sweep indicate she is tracked by End Citizens United and other trackers as having $0 in corporate PAC contributions specifically (as distinct from other PAC money such as labor or ideological PACs). The available record does not support characterizing her as accepting corporate PAC money; her PAC support documented in the dossier comes from labor unions and advocacy groups (EMILY's List, League of Conservation Voters, unions, etc.), not corporate PACs.

inaccurate_statement: Abortion: Stelson strongly supports abortion rights / Perry strongly anti-abortion
description: Presenting Perry as simply 'strongly anti-abortion' omits that his stated personal position includes exceptions for rape, incest, and life of the mother, and that he supports IVF access and co-introduced the IVF Protection Act, even though he also currently cosponsors the Life at Conception Act, which contains no such exceptions and defines personhood from the moment of fertilization. His record on this issue is genuinely conflicting rather than a simple, one-sided 'strongly anti-abortion, no exceptions' position, and presenting only one side risks misleading readers about his actual documented stance.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supported Texas's lawsuit seeking to invalidate Biden's certified victories in Pennsylvania and other states
description: No record in the available material documents Perry personally supporting or joining the Texas v. Pennsylvania lawsuit (filed by Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton seeking to invalidate results in Pennsylvania, Georgia, Michigan, and Wisconsin). Perry's documented 2020-election-related actions center on the Jeffrey Clark scheme, phone seizure, and his January 6 certification vote, not this specific lawsuit. This appears to be an unsupported addition not found in the documented record.

inaccurate_statement: A 2024 Pennsylvania court filing stated that Perry was engaged with election deniers working to provide alternative elector slates and specifically described his involvement in efforts to present an alternative Pennsylvania slate
description: No record in the available material corroborates a 2024 Pennsylvania court filing describing Perry's involvement in a fake-elector scheme or an alternative Pennsylvania elector slate. The documented record instead centers on the Jeffrey Clark installation effort, the FBI phone seizure, and the January 6 vote; no fake-electors connection to Perry is documented in the available research.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supported a lawsuit brought by Texas seeking to invalidate Pennsylvania's and three other states' certified electoral votes
description: No record exists of Perry personally supporting or being involved in the Texas v. Pennsylvania lawsuit (Texas Attorney General's suit seeking to invalidate results in Pennsylvania, Georgia, Michigan, and Wisconsin). The documented record of Perry's 2020-election-related conduct centers on the FBI phone seizure, the Jeffrey Clark matter, and his January 6, 2021 vote against certifying Arizona's and Pennsylvania's electoral votes — not backing of the Texas lawsuit, which is a distinct legal action brought by a state attorney general, not by individual members of Congress.

inaccurate_statement: A federal judge ordered Perry to turn over more than 1,600 emails and texts to the FBI, while allowing him to withhold 396 communications protected by the Speech or Debate Clause
description: The documented figures are that a D.C. Circuit ruling permitted access to 1,659 of the roughly 2,219 contested messages by December 2023 — the number and framing in the response are close to but not precisely matching the confirmed figures, and courts allowed access to the large majority of contested messages rather than a clean '1,600 turned over, 396 withheld' split as stated.

inaccurate_statement: A Pennsylvania court filing describes Perry as being involved in efforts to provide an alternative/fake slate of electors with the objective of changing the certified result
description: No record exists of Perry being tied to a fake-elector scheme specifically; the documented controversy centers on his role in the Jeffrey Clark matter and phone-seizure litigation, not an alternate-electors effort, and no such court filing linking him to fake electors is referenced in available material.

inaccurate_statement: A voter questionnaire specifically asked whether Stelson supports redirecting police-department funds to community programs, and the listing shows she did not answer
description: No record exists of any voter questionnaire specifically asking Stelson about redirecting police funds to community programs, nor any record of her declining to answer such a question. This appears to be a fabricated detail not grounded in any actual questionnaire or survey.

inaccurate_statement: In the 2024 cycle, his campaign reported about $4.5 million raised, with the majority coming from individual contributions and hundreds of thousands from PACs
description: The confirmed FEC-verified figure for Perry's committee (Patriots for Perry) covers the period January 2025–June 2026, showing total receipts of about $5,194,925.35, not $4.5 million for the 2024 cycle specifically. No figure in the available records matches a $4.5 million total for the 2024 cycle; individual contributions ($3,100,218.61 of $5,194,925.35, or about 60%) and PAC contributions ($650,127, about 12.5%) are confirmed for the 2025-2026 filing period, so while the general shape (majority from individuals, meaningful PAC share) is roughly consistent with the confirmed data, the specific $4.5 million 2024-cycle figure is not supported.

inaccurate_statement: The campaign reported no candidate loans
description: The financial disclosure data shows Stelson's committee reported total receipts, disbursements, and cash on hand figures, but the knowledge base does not mention candidate loans one way or the other for her committee specifically (it does note this detail was confirmed absent for Perry's committee). Since the knowledge base doesn't affirmatively address whether Stelson's committee reported any loans, this can't be confirmed as accurate, and given it's a specific quantifiable claim not verified in the available material, it should be treated with caution rather than accepted at face value.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson subsequently lost to Scott Perry by roughly 6,000 votes
description: Stelson lost to Perry by approximately 5,000 to 5,133 votes (a roughly 1.2-point margin), not roughly 6,000 votes as stated.

inaccurate_statement: Later-unsealed messages showed Perry telling Clark, shortly before January 6, "You are the man. I have confirmed it."
description: No record of this specific quote attributed to Perry exists in the available documentation of his communications with Jeffrey Clark. The dossier documents the Jeffrey Clark episode, the phone seizure, and the litigation over which messages could be reviewed, but does not corroborate this specific quoted text, which appears to be a fabricated or misattributed detail.

inaccurate_statement: 396 of the phone communications were protected by congressional privilege
description: The documented figure is that a court ruling permitted access to 1,659 of approximately 2,219 contested messages by December 2023; the remaining protected count is not confirmed in available material as exactly 396, making this specific breakdown unverified against the documented figures.

inaccurate_statement: In December 2023, a federal judge authorized investigators to access 1,659 of 2,055 disputed records while withholding 396
description: The number of contested phone records is documented as approximately 2,219, not 2,055. The figure of 1,659 records to which access was granted by December 2023 is accurate, but the total pool of disputed documents (and the corresponding withheld count) is misstated.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson spent more than 30 years as a broadcast journalist in Pennsylvania, including many years as an anchor for WGAL-TV
description: Stelson's broadcast journalism career spanned nearly 40 years overall, but her specific tenure at WGAL-TV (the Pennsylvania anchor role referenced) was 26 years (1997–2023), not 'more than 30 years.' She also worked at other stations (WHTM-TV, WHP-TV Harrisburg, WPLG-TV Miami, WITF) that were not all in Pennsylvania, so the '30 years in Pennsylvania' framing overstates her specific WGAL/Pennsylvania tenure, though her overall journalism career length (nearly 40 years) is separately and accurately noted elsewhere in the response.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson proposes encouraging new home construction, reducing permitting barriers, addressing corporate/Wall Street purchases of homes, and expanding access to affordable housing.
description: Stelson's documented housing platform supports federal investment in affordable housing and increasing housing availability, but no source shows her proposing specific mechanisms like reducing permitting barriers or addressing corporate/Wall Street home purchases; these specific policy mechanisms are not found in her platform materials.

inaccurate_statement: He served three terms in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives, from 2006–2012
description: Scott Perry served in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives from 2007 to 2012, not 2006 to 2012, per his confirmed biography.

inaccurate_statement: He commanded units at the company level
description: Available records document Perry's command of a battalion (2nd Battalion, 104th Aviation Regiment) and later a regiment/brigade-level unit, but do not confirm a company-level command specifically; this appears to be an added detail not supported by the record.

inaccurate_statement: He is currently serving his seventh consecutive Congress (119th Congress, 2025–2027)
description: Perry has served continuously in the U.S. House since January 2013, spanning the 113th through 119th Congresses — that is seven Congresses total, which matches the '119th Congress' being his seventh; this claim appears to actually be accurate on closer count (113th, 114th, 115th, 116th, 117th, 118th, 119th = 7), so it is not an error.

inaccurate_statement: Perry says abortion policy should largely be left to the states
description: Perry's documented position on abortion is not framed around leaving the matter to the states. His campaign site states he believes in 'the sanctity of Life – period' with exceptions for rape, incest, and life of the mother, and he is a longtime cosponsor of the federal Life at Conception Act, which would establish a national fetal-personhood standard from the moment of fertilization — the opposite of a states'-rights framing. This response omits his cosponsorship of that federal bill and the resulting conflict with his stated support for exceptions and IVF, presenting only a partial, states'-rights characterization not supported by the record.

inaccurate_statement: His priorities include banning sanctuary cities.
description: No record exists of Perry making sanctuary-city bans a stated priority; his documented immigration platform centers on border security, enforcement metrics, legal-immigration reform, and visa policy, with no mention of sanctuary cities specifically.

inaccurate_statement: He supports making the VA more accountable, expanding veterans' education benefits, increasing healthcare options, and improving treatment for PTSD.
description: There is no documented record of Perry stating these specific veterans-policy planks (VA accountability, expanded education benefits, PTSD treatment improvements); his veterans-related record as documented centers on other legislative activity not matching this specific list.

inaccurate_statement: He supports federal tax credits for private and religious-school scholarships (school choice).
description: No record of Perry taking this specific school-choice/tax-credit-scholarship position was found; this appears to be a generic Republican platform inference presented as his specific stated position without support.

inaccurate_statement: In an August 2026 campaign message, he described his biggest priority as representing his constituents, while highlighting energy costs and the tax cuts enacted by Republicans.
description: No such specific August 2026 campaign message with this framing is documented; this appears to be an invented or unverifiable specific claim not grounded in any confirmed source.

inaccurate_statement: She has called for an expanded VA hospital/medical system
description: No source documents Stelson calling for an expanded VA hospital or medical system specifically; her documented veterans position focuses on expanding access to health benefits, education, and job training, not a stated plan to expand VA hospital infrastructure.

inaccurate_statement: Her current platform supports an age cap for members of Congress
description: Stelson's own quote hedges this as 'maybe age limits,' not a firmly stated platform position; presenting it as a definite current platform item overstates her documented level of commitment to this specific policy.

inaccurate_statement: Served nearly 40 years in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard
description: Perry served in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard from 1980 to 2019, which is approximately 39 years — close to but not quite "nearly 40 years" is roughly accurate, though this is a borderline/minor rounding issue rather than a clear contradiction.

inaccurate_statement: Perry served nearly 40 years in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard
description: Perry served in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard from 1980 to 2019, which is approximately 39 years — this is close to accurate and essentially correct, though it rounds up slightly; however, this is a minor detail not worth flagging as a substantive error.

inaccurate_statement: Perry is currently serving his seventh House term
description: Perry was first elected to the U.S. House in 2012 and took office in January 2013. Counting terms from the 113th Congress (2013-2015) through the 119th Congress (2025-2027), which would be his seventh two-year term, this is actually accurate — 113th, 114th, 115th, 116th, 117th, 118th, 119th Congresses are seven terms. This statement is correct, not an error.

inaccurate_statement: He served nearly 40 years in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard
description: Perry served in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard from 1980 to 2019, which is approximately 39 years — close to the stated figure, but he grew up in central Pennsylvania (Dillsburg area, York County) and the knowledge base notes he was actually born in San Diego, California, not central Pennsylvania as implied by the response's framing that he 'grew up in central Pennsylvania.' The Guard service length itself (about 39 years) is roughly accurate and not the core issue; the inaccuracy is the claim he 'grew up in' central Pennsylvania when he was born in San Diego (though records show he attended high school in Dillsburg, PA, so this is a minor, ambiguous point rather than a clear contradiction).

inaccurate_statement: He served as chairman of the House Freedom Caucus from 2021 to 2023
description: Available records indicate Perry chaired the House Freedom Caucus from 2022 to 2024, not 2021 to 2023.

inaccurate_statement: Her campaign noted that Perry was the only member of Pennsylvania's congressional delegation to vote against one such housing bill
description: The housing bill (21st Century ROAD to Housing Act) passed the House 396-13, with Perry among 13 opposing votes nationally; while other reporting confirms Perry was the only Pennsylvania delegation member to vote no, the response's framing implying this detail specifically came from Stelson's campaign is unverified, and the vote count context (13 not 32) matters for accuracy of the broader claim, though this specific 'only PA member' detail is separately documented as accurate elsewhere.

inaccurate_statement: During their 2024 debate, Perry said, "If you're going to represent the district and raise our taxes, you should live here."
description: No source in the available research confirms this exact quote being said by Perry during the 2024 debate. While Perry did criticize Stelson's out-of-district residency as a real, documented line of attack, this specific quoted wording is not verifiable against the documented record and appears to be an invented or embellished quote attributed to him.

inaccurate_statement: After narrowly defeating Stelson in 2024, Perry said her campaign had been powered by out-of-state donors, complaining that people from the West Coast had poured millions into the district despite not knowing or caring about the area
description: No record in the available research supports this specific post-election quote or claim about West Coast donors attributed to Perry. While Stelson did outraise Perry with a large share of individual contributions, this particular framed complaint about West Coast money is not corroborated by any documented source.

inaccurate_statement: In 2025, his spokesman said she supported raising taxes by more than $2,000 on working Pennsylvanians.
description: The tax-related quote attributed to Perry's campaign about raising taxes by more than $2,000 on Pennsylvanians is real, but it came in response to Stelson's April 2026 gas-price criticism, not in 2025 as the response states. The substance of the claim is accurate; only the year is wrong.

inaccurate_statement: The current Medicare Part D annual out-of-pocket cap is $2,100
description: The Inflation Reduction Act established a $2,000 annual out-of-pocket cap for Medicare Part D drug costs (confirmed in the dossier's description of the IRA provisions Perry sought to repeal), not $2,100 as stated in the response. This is a minor numerical error about a general Medicare policy fact, not something specific to either candidate's record.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supports a broad energy portfolio, including clean-energy technologies, arguing that energy development can create jobs while reducing energy costs.
description: Perry's platform emphasizes an "all-of-the-above" energy strategy centered on conventional sources (oil, gas, hydropower) and has been described as opposing federal clean-energy subsidies and incentives, including votes that reduced them. Characterizing his energy plank as including support for "clean-energy technologies" as a jobs driver is not supported and runs counter to his documented opposition to clean-energy subsidies.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supported the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act, which sought to align federal job-training programs with local employers and economic-development needs
description: No record in the available material shows Perry's position on or support for the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act. His documented jobs/workforce statements focus on deregulation, tax policy, and general references to unfilled manufacturing job openings, not this specific piece of legislation, which predates his more recent documented platform positions.

inaccurate_statement: An economic-impact study estimated the Three Mile Island restart could create 3,400 direct and indirect jobs
description: No specific jobs figure of 3,400 direct and indirect jobs tied to the Three Mile Island/Crane Clean Energy Center restart is documented in the available material. Perry's confirmed statement on this topic is a general endorsement of the restart for job creation and reduced dependence on foreign energy, without this specific numerical estimate.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's congressional committee has jurisdiction over flood-damage reduction, disaster preparedness, the Army Corps of Engineers and related water infrastructure.
description: Perry's subcommittee, Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management, has jurisdiction over disaster preparedness, mitigation, response and recovery under the Stafford Act and FEMA/DHS emergency management matters — but flood-damage reduction and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers civil-works activities actually fall under the separate Water Resources and Environment subcommittee, which Perry does not chair or sit on. The response conflates the jurisdictions of these two distinct subcommittees.

inaccurate_statement: The House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee (or its subcommittee Perry chairs) has jurisdiction over flood-damage reduction, and Perry as chairman of the relevant subcommittee has examined FEMA's Flood Mitigation Assistance and BRIC programs
description: Perry chairs the Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management subcommittee, which has jurisdiction over FEMA/disaster preparedness and response under the Stafford Act, but flood-damage reduction and Army Corps of Engineers civil works matters actually fall under the separate Water Resources and Environment subcommittee. The response conflates these two subcommittees' jurisdictions, though the broader point that Perry has engaged with FEMA mitigation policy oversight is consistent with his committee role.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry's official site cited as 'Scott Perry's Official Site' link (implying scottperry.com or similar as his official site)
description: Scott Perry's actual 2026 campaign site is patriotsforperry.com. A commonly guessed domain, scottperry.com, belongs to an unrelated private car enthusiast and has no connection to the congressman. The response's repeated citation of an unspecified 'Scott Perry's Official Site' link without clarity risks this confusion, though the exact URL used isn't specified in the response text.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supported the STOP School Violence Act, which included funding for school security technology, threat assessment teams, crisis intervention programs, and better coordination between schools and law enforcement.
description: No record of Perry's public safety platform mentions the STOP School Violence Act or school safety measures. His documented public safety positions are limited to law-enforcement support under Second Amendment and Defense/National Security framing, with no dedicated school-safety plank found in his House.gov issues pages or campaign site materials.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has expressed support for measures involving transparency, accountability, and training while opposing proposals he believed would reduce law enforcement effectiveness.
description: No documented statement from Perry addresses police transparency, accountability, or training reforms specifically. His confirmed record shows opposition to new gun restrictions and general law-enforcement support (e.g., a social-media line about supporting law enforcement using tools to 'get the bad guys'), but no source discusses accountability/training measures as described here.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's broader public safety positions have emphasized preventing violence, addressing threats before they escalate, and supporting security measures.
description: This is a vague, unsupported characterization not tied to any documented statement. Research specifically found no dedicated, current public-safety/crime plank on Perry's House.gov or campaign site; the closest adjacent content is under Second Amendment and Defense/National Security categories, not a violence-prevention framing as described.

inaccurate_statement: In June 2026, Perry participated in a South-Central Pennsylvania FBI discussion focused on information sharing and partnerships to improve public safety
description: A review of Perry's official House press release archive (which lists releases continuously from January through August 2026) shows no June 2026 press release or event about an FBI discussion on information sharing/partnerships for public safety. The only related, verifiable event is a March 2026 roundtable Perry co-hosted with House Intelligence Committee Chairman Rick Crawford in Carlisle, PA, which included FBI representatives, but that event was focused on Chinese Communist Party counterintelligence threats, not general 'information sharing and partnerships to improve public safety,' and it occurred in March, not June 2026. No other search results corroborate a distinct June 2026 FBI discussion event tied to Perry. Given the specificity of the claim (exact month, exact FBI theme) and the failure to find any supporting evidence despite a thorough search of his own official communications, this appears to be a fabricated or conflated claim. It is scored as minor severity since it may reflect a mixed-up date/topic version of a real, similar event (the March 2026 FBI-related roundtable) rather than a wholesale invention of Perry's engagement with the FBI on public safety topics.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supported the 2017 Border Security for America Act, which called for funding walls/fencing, other barriers, technology and air assets along the southern border, including hiring 5,000 additional Border Patrol agents and 5,000 CBP officers, biometric entry/exit systems, and Stonegarden program funding
description: The knowledge base documents Perry's confirmed immigration/border legislative record as centering on his own stated House.gov platform language (securing the border first, DHS metrics, technology use) and specific named bills he cosponsored in the 2020s (Permanent Trump Secure Border Act, Secure the Border Act/H.R. 2, One Nation One Visa Policy Act, etc.). There is no mention anywhere in his dossier of the 2017 Border Security for America Act or any specific personnel figures (5,000 Border Patrol agents, 5,000 CBP officers) or Stonegarden program funding attributed to him. While Perry has consistently supported border-security-first policies generally, these specific bill citations and numbers are not corroborated and appear to be invented or drawn from a generic template rather than his documented record.
