description: Perry's documented healthcare positions include reconciliation-bill Medicaid work requirements, cosponsoring repeal of Inflation Reduction Act drug-pricing provisions, and standard GOP-style ACA criticism (interstate insurance sales, HSA expansion, tort reform) on dated issue pages, but there is no confirmed record of him currently supporting outright ACA repeal as a 2025-2026 position; the characterization overstates his documented stance without direct sourcing for a repeal push.

inaccurate_statement: Perry opposes some measures aimed at reducing Medicare out-of-pocket costs
description: This is a vague, unsupported generalization; the documented record shows a more nuanced picture, including that Perry previously backed legislation (H.R. 19) that would have capped Medicare insulin costs and out-of-pocket drug costs, which cuts against a blanket claim that he opposes measures reducing Medicare out-of-pocket costs.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson explicitly says law enforcement should be treated with respect while also being held to constitutional standards, implying her gun-violence position 'isn't simply more gun restrictions' and instead emphasizes constitutional limits on police power.
description: No source shows Stelson framing her public-safety position around constitutional limits on police power. Her documented platform (via GIFFORDS' endorsement and tracker materials) is explicitly restriction-focused: expanding background checks, red flag laws, safe storage incentives, removing ghost guns, and disarming domestic abusers, with no countervailing emphasis on constitutional limits on police power. This specific framing has been identified as fabricated in prior research.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's position on police 'isn't simply more gun restrictions'; she emphasizes constitutional policing and accountability alongside supporting resources for officers
description: Stelson's documented public-safety platform, per her endorsement from GIFFORDS and other trackers, centers explicitly on expanding gun restrictions — background checks for all gun sales, red flag laws, safe storage incentives, and removing ghost guns — with no found source describing a countervailing emphasis on 'constitutional limits on police power' or a framing that her approach 'isn't simply more gun restrictions.' This framing fabricates a nuanced, accountability-first position that isn't supported by her actual documented platform and misrepresents the emphasis of her stance, which is central to the response's core comparison.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson explicitly supports providing resources for law enforcement while emphasizing constitutional policing and accountability
description: No source shows Stelson framing her public-safety position around 'constitutional policing' or limits on police power as a counterweight to gun restrictions. Her documented platform, sourced to GIFFORDS and other trackers, centers explicitly on expanding gun restrictions (background checks, red-flag laws, safe storage, ghost-gun enforcement) with no mention of a 'constitutional policing' framing.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry has supported banning sanctuary cities
description: No record in the available material documents Scott Perry specifically supporting a sanctuary-city ban as part of his platform. His documented immigration positions focus on border security metrics, technology, legal immigration reform, and enforcement legislation like the Secure the Border Act and Permanent Trump Secure Border Act, but a sanctuary-cities plank is not among the confirmed items.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has taken a more skeptical position toward data centers in PA-10, saying he doesn't think the district is the best location for them.
description: Perry's actual documented statement on data centers is that regulation and siting decisions are local-municipality matters outside his federal purview ("I don't get into local zoning and building... those are local decisions"), not that he is skeptical of data centers being sited in the district or thinks it isn't a good location for them. Characterizing this as opposition or skepticism mischaracterizes his stated hands-off/neutral position.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's published priorities emphasize broader affordability and governance issues rather than a detailed roads-and-bridges plan.
description: Stelson has made specific, documented statements on roads and bridges, including calling for investment in roads, bridges, public transportation and the electric grid, specifically highlighting the I-83 South Bridge project, and criticizing Perry for voting against the infrastructure law that funded it. Characterizing her platform as lacking any 'detailed roads-and-bridges plan' understates this documented record, even though she has not released a comprehensive standalone infrastructure white paper.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's public statements have highlighted concerns about flash flooding and climate-related severe storms, suggesting support for resilience investments
description: No direct statement from Stelson specifically on flood management or flash flooding was found despite dedicated research; this remains a confirmed gap in her documented platform, not a sourced position.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's record shows he did not have a specific PA-10 flood-management initiative matching a large federal investment approach (implying he has taken no action on flood-related infrastructure)
description: While no dedicated flood-management statement from Perry was found, he has been engaged in disaster-mitigation and FEMA-related oversight work generally, and PennDOT's current I-83 project (which he has advocated for) includes flood-related Mill Creek relocation work, complicating a flat claim that he has no flood-management engagement.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson says she supports funding and resources for law enforcement to do their jobs safely, while also emphasizing constitutional policing
description: Stelson's documented public-safety platform centers explicitly on expanding gun restrictions (background checks, red flag laws, safe storage incentives, removing ghost guns, community violence intervention) rather than on a 'constitutional policing' counterbalance theme. A dedicated check found no source supporting this framing and found it contradicts her well-documented restriction-focused platform.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson supports the Second Amendment but says people with dangerous backgrounds or other disqualifying circumstances shouldn't have guns
description: This undersells Stelson's actual documented gun-safety platform, which explicitly calls for expanding background checks to all gun sales, implementing red flag laws, incentivizing safe storage, and removing ghost guns from circulation — a broader restriction-focused position than the narrower framing given here.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson says she supports law enforcement and providing officers the resources to do their jobs safely, while also emphasizing constitutional accountability
description: Research into Stelson's actual documented public-safety position found no support for framing it around 'constitutional accountability' or limits on police power as a countervailing theme to gun restrictions. Her well-documented platform, including her GIFFORDS endorsement, centers explicitly on expanding gun restrictions (universal background checks, red flag laws, safe storage requirements, ghost gun restrictions), not on a constitutional-accountability counterbalance to law enforcement resources. This framing appears to mischaracterize her actual position, though it doesn't reverse the broader accurate point that she supports law enforcement resources and gun-safety measures.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson says she supports funding law enforcement so officers can do their jobs safely, while emphasizing constitutional accountability.
description: No source shows Stelson framing her position with an emphasis on 'constitutional accountability' or limits on police power alongside funding law enforcement. Her documented platform centers on expanding gun restrictions (background checks, red flag laws, safe storage, ghost gun enforcement) without this specific 'constitutional accountability' framing being attributed to her by any source.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson says an 'all-of-the-above' approach including wind and solar can lower energy costs
description: The 'all-of-the-above' energy framing is Perry's documented terminology, not Stelson's. Stelson's platform is described as supporting expanded clean-energy investment and renewables, but there is no record of her using the specific 'all-of-the-above' phrase, which risks confusing the two candidates' framing.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supports what he calls a 'blended energy portfolio'
description: Perry's documented energy platform describes an 'all-of-the-above' strategy including hydropower and continued oil/gas development, not a 'blended energy portfolio.' No source uses this specific phrase for him.

inaccurate_statement: Janelle Stelson supports an "all-of-the-above" energy strategy that includes wind and solar
description: The "all-of-the-above" energy strategy framing is documented as Scott Perry's stated platform (including hydropower and continued oil/gas development), not Stelson's. Stelson's documented energy positions instead emphasize expanding renewable/clean energy investment and diversifying supply, but there is no record of her using or being described with the specific "all-of-the-above" label.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's stated position is that officers need resources to do their jobs safely, while also emphasizing constitutional policing
description: No source shows Stelson framing her public-safety position around emphasizing constitutional limits on policing power. Her documented platform, including her GIFFORDS-tracked positions, centers on expanding gun restrictions (background checks, red flag laws, safe storage, ghost-gun enforcement) rather than a 'constitutional policing' framing, and this specific characterization has been found unsupported and contradictory to her actual documented stance.

inaccurate_statement: A 2026 voter guide summarizes Perry's position as helping small businesses access capital and cutting through red tape, while supporting rural broadband
description: This description closely matches Stelson's own platform language (helping with SBA loans, cutting through red tape, and a rural broadband plank), not Perry's. Perry's confirmed small-business platform emphasizes generic tax/regulatory relief and cites unnamed business owners' feedback, with no specific mention of capital-access help or rural broadband; that specific combination of points is documented as Stelson's platform, not Perry's.

inaccurate_statement: Janelle Stelson — I found no clear public statement from her campaign specifically calling for a moratorium or taking a strong anti-data-center-development position... I did not find a detailed data-center policy.
description: Stelson has made a direct, on-record statement about data centers: she said the issue is 'nudging right up against the family home that they've had for a long time or the family farm,' and reporting indicates she supports letting local governments say no to data-center projects until residents' concerns are addressed. Claiming no such statement exists is a clear factual error on the central question the prompt asked.

inaccurate_statement: Janelle Stelson has explicitly criticized Perry for supporting federal tax breaks for data-center companies, framed as a vote for a 'massive tax break' for the industry
description: No record exists of Stelson criticizing Perry for a specific vote on a 'massive tax break' for data centers. Her documented data-center-related criticism, per CNBC (Apr. 24, 2026), centers on the impact of data centers on neighborhoods/family farms and support for local governments' ability to say no to projects, not a specific tax-break vote by Perry.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry voted for a 'massive tax break' for the data-center industry
description: No documented vote or record shows Perry supporting or voting for a specific 'massive tax break' for data centers. His documented position (CNBC, Apr. 2026) is that data-center zoning/regulation is a local, not federal, matter outside his purview — a framing of non-involvement, not an affirmative tax-break vote.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson has held public-facing events but there isn't enough documentation to confidently say she holds substantially more town halls than Perry, and my search did not turn up a comparable series of recent, open-to-public town halls hosted by Perry
description: The available record actually does support a clear, well-documented asymmetry: multiple independent outlets (Spotlight PA, AP News, ABC27, Pennsylvania Capital-Star) confirm Perry has not held an in-person town hall since July 30, 2019, over 2,000 days as of 2025 reporting, and instead relies on telephone town halls. Stelson has directly and repeatedly criticized Perry as 'a coward' for avoiding in-person town halls. The response hedges as if this comparison is essentially undocumented or a toss-up, when in fact there is a specific, well-sourced pattern showing Perry avoids in-person town halls while Stelson has been more publicly accessible; the hedged uncertainty understates the strength of the documented evidence on this specific question.

inaccurate_statement: Democratic Jewish Outreach Pennsylvania endorsed Stelson.
description: The Pennsylvania-specific group Democratic Jewish Outreach Pennsylvania had not formally issued endorsements for this cycle; the group that actually endorsed Stelson was the separate national organization Jewish Democratic Council of America (JDCA). This appears to be a mix-up between two similarly named but distinct Jewish Democratic organizations.

inaccurate_statement: Democratic Jewish Outreach Pennsylvania endorsed Stelson.
description: Democratic Jewish Outreach Pennsylvania (DJOP) had not formally endorsed Stelson; the group's chair stated it had not yet begun formal endorsement evaluations for the cycle. The organization that publicly endorsed Stelson was a separate national group, the Jewish Democratic Council of America (JDCA), which appears to have been confused with DJOP here.

inaccurate_statement: The main candidates in the PA-10 race are Scott Perry and Democratic candidates including Janelle Stelson and Justin Douglas.
description: Justin Douglas was Stelson's opponent in the Democratic primary and was defeated by her 67.4%–32.6%; he is not on the November 2026 general-election ballot. Presenting him as a current general-election candidate alongside Stelson and Perry misstates the current field, though it does not change the core Perry-vs-Stelson matchup being described.

inaccurate_statement: The main candidates in the PA-10 race are Scott Perry and Democratic candidates including Janelle Stelson and Justin Douglas.
description: Justin Douglas was Stelson's opponent in the Democratic primary and was defeated by her 67.4%–32.6%; he is not on the November 2026 general-election ballot. Presenting him as a current general-election candidate alongside Stelson and Perry misstates the current field, though it does not change the core Perry-vs-Stelson matchup being described.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's transfers/other receipts were about $959,584 (15.1%)
description: Stelson's transfers from other authorized committees were documented as $937,128.56 (~15%), not $959,584. This is a minor numerical discrepancy against the confirmed FEC breakdown.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's transfers and other receipts were $1.44M (27.7%)
description: Perry's transfers from other authorized committees were documented as $1,428,197.30 (~27.5%), close to but not exactly matching the $1.44M/27.7% figure cited; a minor numerical discrepancy.

inaccurate_statement: Among the largest political committees giving directly to Stelson is the Machinists' PAC ($10,000)
description: No evidence exists of any endorsement or contribution connection between the International Association of Machinists (IAM) and Janelle Stelson's campaign; dedicated research into her union endorsements and donor base found no mention of IAM or a Machinists' PAC contribution, suggesting this specific claim is fabricated.

inaccurate_statement: The largest direct PAC donor identified in the available data for Perry is Club for Growth PAC, at roughly $50,900
description: Federal law caps what a multicandidate PAC like Club for Growth PAC can contribute directly to a single candidate's committee at $5,000 per election (typically $10,000 combined for primary and general). A figure of $50,900 given directly to Perry's campaign committee in one cycle would be roughly five times the legal contribution ceiling and is not supported by available FEC data, indicating this specific figure is fabricated even though Club for Growth PAC is a real backer of Perry.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's largest direct PAC contributor was Club for Growth PAC, at about $15,800 in itemized contributions
description: Club for Growth is indeed a top contributor to Perry's campaigns, but across every election cycle checked (2018, 2020, 2023-2024), OpenSecrets/FEC data show these contributions are attributed entirely to individuals bundled through Club for Growth's network, with $0 coming from the PAC itself (e.g., Club for Growth totals of $51,887, $115,171, and $96,817 in various cycles, all listed as '$0' under 'PACs'). Direct PAC-to-candidate contributions are also capped at $5,000 per election under FEC rules, making a $15,800 direct PAC contribution from a single PAC in one cycle implausible without conduit/bundling being involved (which is exactly what OpenSecrets classifies as individual money, not PAC money). Thus, the claim's core framing—that Club for Growth PAC directly gave ~$15,800 in itemized PAC contributions—misstates how this money is categorized. The broader point that Club for Growth is a major, closely-linked backer of Perry is accurate, but the specific 'direct PAC contribution' amount and classification appears to be a factual/technical error rather than reflecting the real funding mechanism (individual bundled contributions), so this is a minor inaccuracy rather than one that would change the overall takeaway about Perry's relationship with Club for Growth.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson advocates for investments in renewable energy sources like wind and solar to lower costs and supports tightening environmental regulations
description: No direct statement was found of Stelson specifically naming wind and solar or proposing to tighten environmental regulations; her documented position emphasizes general support for expanding clean-energy investment and diversifying energy sources to lower costs, without the specific 'tightening environmental regulations' framing or naming wind/solar specifically. This presents a more specific policy mechanism than what is actually confirmed on the record.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson advocates for an all-of-the-above energy strategy incorporating renewable sources like wind and solar to lower costs and address climate change
description: The 'all-of-the-above' energy strategy label is Scott Perry's stated platform framing (an all-of-the-above approach including hydropower and continued oil/gas development), not Stelson's. Stelson's platform emphasizes expanding clean-energy investment and lowering costs, but she is not documented as branding her approach 'all-of-the-above.'

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry generally favors leaving abortion regulations up to individual states
description: Perry's documented record does not show him favoring a states'-rights approach to abortion. He is a current cosponsor of the federal Life at Conception Act, which would establish a nationwide constitutional right to life from the moment of fertilization — a federal personhood law, not a policy of deferring abortion regulation to individual states. His campaign site also states a personal position with rape/incest/life-of-mother exceptions, again a personal stance rather than a 'leave it to the states' framework. This characterization mischaracterizes his actual legislative position.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supports leaving abortion regulations primarily to state legislatures
description: Perry's record on abortion is a federal-level cosponsorship matter, not a states'-rights framing. He currently cosponsors the federal Life at Conception Act (H.R. 722), which would establish a federal constitutional right to life from the moment of fertilization with no exceptions for rape, incest, or life of the mother — a national personhood standard, not a position of deferring the issue to individual states. His campaign site separately states a personal position supportive of rape/incest/life exceptions and IVF access. Describing his position as 'leaving abortion regulations primarily to state legislatures' omits this documented federal cosponsorship record and presents only a partial, more moderate-sounding characterization of a genuinely conflicting record.

inaccurate_statement: Perry maintains a pro-life stance, emphasizing the protection of the unborn while supporting exceptions and leaving specific regulations largely up to individual states
description: This presents only one side of Perry's genuinely conflicting record on abortion. While his campaign site does state he supports exceptions for rape, incest, and life of the mother, he is also a current cosponsor of the Life at Conception Act, which contains no such exceptions and defines personhood from the moment of fertilization — a position that conflicts with 'leaving specific regulations largely up to individual states' framing and with his stated exceptions. Presenting only the exceptions-supportive framing without noting this contradiction is a one-sided characterization of a documented conflict, not a fabrication of either individual fact.

inaccurate_statement: Perry maintains a pro-life position, supporting state-level decision-making on abortion.
description: There is no documented statement from Perry framing his abortion position around leaving the issue to states. His actual legislative record shows he currently cosponsors the federal Life at Conception Act, which would establish a national, federal personhood standard from the moment of fertilization with no rape/incest/life-of-mother exceptions — the opposite of a 'leave it to the states' approach. His stated personal position (with rape/incest/life exceptions) also doesn't mention states' rights specifically. Describing his position as 'state-level decision-making' mischaracterizes his documented federal legislative record, though the broader characterization of him as pro-life is accurate.

inaccurate_statement: Perry maintains a personal pro-life stance, has previously supported restrictions, and favors leaving the issue primarily to the states.
description: Perry's actual record on this issue is more complicated than 'leaving it to the states' suggests: he is a current cosponsor of the federal Life at Conception Act, which would establish a constitutional right to life from the moment of fertilization nationwide, with no rape/incest/life-of-mother exceptions — a federal personhood measure, not a states'-rights position. His separate, stated personal position does include rape/incest/life exceptions and IVF support, but the response's characterization omits this federal cosponsorship and the conflict it creates, oversimplifying his actual position.

inaccurate_statement: Perry promoted alternative plans including the 'fake electors' scheme
description: The documented record centers on Perry's role in the Jeffrey Clark scheme, contacts with Mark Meadows, and his January 6 certification vote. No source in the available material ties Perry specifically to promoting a 'fake electors' scheme (a separate effort involving alternate slates of electors in swing states) as opposed to the Jeffrey Clark/DOJ pressure campaign. This conflates two distinct post-2020-election strategies and overstates what is documented about Perry's specific role.

inaccurate_statement: Federal investigators and the House January 6 committee concluded that Perry was a key figure in the multi-pronged effort to reverse the outcome
description: While the House January 6 Select Committee did seek to question Perry about his documented role in the Jeffrey Clark effort and he was referred to the House Ethics Committee, the framing that federal investigators and the committee reached a definitive 'concluded' finding overstates the record. Perry declined the committee's request and subpoena, and the ultimate disposition of the ethics referral was never confirmed. No criminal charges were ever filed against him. The claim's framing skips over the fact that whether he personally sought a pardon is conflicting/disputed, and the phone-seizure litigation outcome is more nuanced than a flat 'concluded' finding.

inaccurate_statement: Voting for America is characterized/labeled as a 'dark money' group whose funding bankrolled Stelson's campaign
description: The $45,000 from Voting for America was personal income paid directly to Stelson for podcast work, not a contribution to her campaign committee. Her actual campaign committee (Friends of Janelle Stelson) and leadership PAC are both fully disclosed, ordinary FEC-registered committees, not dark money. Framing this as her 'campaign' being 'bankrolled' by dark money conflates personal income with campaign financing, though the response does note the payment went to her personally rather than her campaign committee, partially mitigating this.

inaccurate_statement: Referring to "Voting for America" as a 'dark money' political group in the context of a campaign finance disclosure issue, and citing Mother Jones as a source for this
description: The $45,000 paid to Stelson by Voting for America was personal income disclosed on her federal financial disclosure form, not a campaign contribution or campaign finance matter — her actual campaign committee and leadership PAC are fully disclosed, ordinary FEC-registered entities and not dark money by any definition. The nonprofit itself not disclosing its donors is a fair 'dark money' framing for that specific entity, but characterizing this as a 'campaign finance disclosure' controversy blurs a distinction the available reporting is careful to draw. Additionally, the confirmed reporting on the exact $45,000 figure traces to Spotlight PA (citing her own financial disclosure and NOTUS's original reporting), not Mother Jones — no Mother Jones reporting on this specific item is documented.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's previous home address was tied to her past marriage to Dr. Steven Houser
description: No record exists of Janelle Stelson having been married to a 'Dr. Steven Houser' or of her Lancaster County residence being tied to such a marriage. This specific personal detail is not supported by any available source and appears to be a fabricated addition.

inaccurate_statement: 'Voting for America' is described as 'a political group with ties to Democratic strategists'
description: Voting for America is documented as a nonprofit founded in June 2024 by DNC/DCCC alumni and a political lawyer, which is broadly consistent with 'ties to Democratic strategists,' but the response omits key confirmed details—namely that this was personal income paid to Stelson (not a campaign contribution) and that the payment is the actual basis of a 'dark money' controversy due to the nonprofit's non-disclosure status. The characterization is imprecise but not wholly contradicted, making this a narrow framing issue rather than a major error.

inaccurate_statement: This made Perry the only sitting member of Congress to have his phone seized in connection with the probe
description: The knowledge base documents Perry's phone seizure in detail but does not state or support the claim that he was the only sitting member of Congress to have a phone seized in connection with the January 6/2020-election investigations; this specific superlative claim is not corroborated by the available material.

inaccurate_statement: Federal courts ultimately ruled that a vast majority of his emails and text messages (over 1,600 records) were not protected legislative acts and had to be turned over to the DOJ
description: The documented figure is that a D.C. Circuit ruling permitted access to 1,659 of roughly 2,219 contested phone documents by December 2023 -- these were phone records/messages, and the number described (over 1,600) is roughly consistent, but the claim's framing as 'emails and text messages' broadens beyond the documented phone-seizure record without clear support.

inaccurate_statement: Activists and voters in Pennsylvania filed legal challenges seeking to disqualify Perry from the ballot under Section 3 of the 14th Amendment
description: No record of a 14th Amendment Section 3 disqualification challenge against Scott Perry appears in the available material; this specific and checkable legal claim is not corroborated by the documented controversy record, which covers the phone seizure, the Jeffrey Clark matter, and the Ethics Committee referral but not any ballot-disqualification lawsuit.

inaccurate_statement: During a congressional hearing in April 2021, Perry questioned a witness using arguments mirroring the 'Great Replacement' theory, suggesting that nonwhite immigrants were being brought into the U.S. to fundamentally alter the electorate and dilute conservative voting power
description: No mention of this alleged 2021 congressional hearing incident, or of Perry promoting 'Great Replacement' rhetoric, appears anywhere in the documented controversy record, which is otherwise detailed and specific about his real controversies (phone seizure, Jeffrey Clark, Ethics referral, town hall avoidance, etc.). This is a serious, uncorroborated allegation that would significantly mislead a reader about the candidate's documented record if untrue.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's congressional campaign drew severe backlash after posting -- and later deleting -- a meme on Facebook featuring antisemitic tropes depicting stereotypically drawn bankers playing Monopoly atop a board supported by bent figures, an image previously traced to a condemned London mural
description: This specific, detailed allegation of an antisemitic social-media post by Perry's campaign does not appear anywhere in the documented record, which covers his controversies in detail (phone seizure, Jeffrey Clark scheme, Ethics referral, Sharia-Free America Caucus membership) but contains no mention of any antisemitic meme controversy. Given the specificity and severity of this claim, its absence from an otherwise thorough documented record raises serious concern that it is fabricated or misattributed.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has faced criticism for remarks downplaying the severity of the January 6 Capitol riot, as well as comments minimizing modern domestic extremist movements
description: No specific statements or remarks by Perry downplaying the January 6 riot or minimizing domestic extremism are documented in the available material, which otherwise covers his January 6-related record (phone seizure, Jeffrey Clark, certification vote) in detail without mentioning such remarks.

inaccurate_statement: 2002 Pennsylvania DEP Incident: while serving as a local businessman, Perry was charged in 2002 with falsifying environmental reports related to chlorine and acidity levels at a sewage plant tied to his company; Perry maintained he was a whistleblower who discovered and reported the plant's maintenance issues to the Pennsylvania DEP
description: No such 2002 environmental charges or DEP incident involving Perry appears anywhere in the documented record, which states that no criminal charges have ever been filed against Perry in connection with any of his documented controversies -- a statement that would be directly contradicted if this 2002 charge were real and confirmed. This specific, detailed fabricated-sounding claim is a serious and uncorroborated allegation that would substantially mislead readers about the candidate's history.

inaccurate_statement: Perry was the only sitting member of Congress to have their phone seized in connection with the probe.
description: The available record on Perry's phone seizure documents it as a significant, well-covered event but does not establish or corroborate the specific claim that he was the only sitting member of Congress to have a phone seized in connection with the broader January 6/2020-election investigation (the 'Arctic Frost' probe). This specific superlative claim is not supported by the documented record.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson spent '26 to 37 years' as a trusted news anchor and reporter
description: Her broadcast anchor tenure at WGAL-TV was 26 years (1997–2023), not a range of '26 to 37 years' — the '37 years' figure appears to be a garbled or fabricated addition, though it doesn't materially change the overall picture of her long journalism career.

inaccurate_statement: She has experience as a small-business owner
description: No record exists of Stelson having been a small-business owner; her documented professional background consists of broadcast journalism, a speechwriting job at the Egyptian Embassy, and her political campaigns, with no mention of owning a small business.

inaccurate_statement: She has experience as a nonprofit leader focusing on community engagement
description: No record exists of Stelson serving as a nonprofit leader; her documented background does not include this role, and this detail appears unsupported.

inaccurate_statement: Advocates for expanding access to child care
description: No source in the available material documents a child-care platform plank for Stelson. Her stated affordability priorities focus on food, gas, housing, prescription drugs, and utilities, plus tax breaks and small-business support, but no child-care-specific policy statement is recorded.

inaccurate_statement: Advocates for raising Pennsylvania's minimum wage above its current rate
description: Stelson has called Pennsylvania's $7.25 minimum wage 'outrageous' and lower than neighboring states, which implies support for raising it, but her documented platform emphasizes vocational training and jobs that 'pay family-supporting wages' rather than a specific stated minimum-wage increase proposal. This is a reasonable but imprecise characterization of her actual framing.

inaccurate_statement: Defending democratic norms and free elections
description: No documented platform plank frames her priorities in terms of 'defending democratic norms and free elections' as a forward-looking policy priority; her documented criticism of Perry centers on his role in 2020 election-related controversies as an attack line, not as a stated first-person 'priority' plank on her own campaign platform.

inaccurate_statement: Founder and owner of Hydrotech Mechanical Services, Inc. since 1993, alongside an early career working as a mechanic, draftsman, and licensed insurance agent
description: Perry's biography describes him as having co-founded a mechanical contracting business and worked as a mechanic, dock worker, draftsman, and licensed insurance agent, but the specific business name 'Hydrotech Mechanical Services, Inc.' and the founding date of 1993 are not supported by the available biographical material, which does not name this specific company.

inaccurate_statement: Retired as a Brigadier General on March 1, 2019
description: The specific retirement date of March 1, 2019 is not confirmed in available records; the dossier states his National Guard service ran 1980–2019 without specifying an exact retirement date. This is a narrow, unverified detail that does not change the overall accurate picture of his military career.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has championed tax-cut legislation, such as the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act
description: The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act was enacted in December 2017. Perry's confirmed tax-related legislative activity in the available record involves cosponsoring more recent measures like the Main Street Tax Certainty Act and supporting the 2025 tax-and-spending law; no record specifically documents his role in championing the 2017 TCJA in particular, though as a sitting House Republican since 2013 he would have voted for it. This is a minor supporting detail that doesn't change the overall accurate picture of his tax-policy priorities.

inaccurate_statement: Supports increasing accountability and oversight for federal immigration enforcement (framed as her immigration platform without further detail)
description: Stelson's actual immigration statements go further than generic 'accountability and oversight,' explicitly calling for ICE agents to wear visible badges and not masks, and for independent investigations into deaths involving ICE agents; the response's vaguer framing is not contradicted but is an incomplete characterization rather than an error, though it doesn't misstate a documented position.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson supports a 5-year Farm Bill
description: Stelson's platform calls for a 'new Farm Bill' aimed at lowering farmers' input costs and enabling right-to-repair for equipment, but no source specifies a '5-year' duration for her proposed Farm Bill; this specific detail is not documented in her platform materials.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has introduced legislation targeting renewable energy, electric vehicles, and ethanol subsidies—such as the Restoring Energy Market Freedom Act, the Restoring Fuel Market Freedom Act, and the Restoring Vehicle Freedom Act
description: No record exists of Perry introducing bills with these specific titles. The knowledge base documents Perry's actual energy-related legislative actions, including his 2025 bill to eliminate the Renewable Fuel Standard and his support for legislation eliminating clean-energy, EV, and ethanol subsidies, but no bill named 'Restoring Energy Market Freedom Act,' 'Restoring Fuel Market Freedom Act,' or 'Restoring Vehicle Freedom Act' appears in his documented record. This is a narrow detail about specific bill titles rather than a mischaracterization of his overall energy stance, which is otherwise accurately described.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supports policies requiring proof of citizenship for voter registration
description: No documented record shows Perry sponsoring, cosponsoring, or making a direct statement supporting proof-of-citizenship voter registration requirements. This is a specific, checkable claim not found in his documented legislative record or platform statements.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supports leaving abortion regulations up to individual states rather than enacting a federal ban
description: This presents only one side of a genuinely conflicting record. While Perry's campaign site states a personal pro-life position with exceptions for rape, incest, and life of the mother, and does not call for a federal ban outright, he is also a current cosponsor of the federal Life at Conception Act (H.R. 722), which would establish a federal constitutional right to life from the moment of fertilization with no exceptions for rape, incest, or life of the mother—a national measure, not a states'-rights approach. Presenting his position as simply deferring to states, without noting this cosponsorship, gives a materially incomplete and misleading picture of his actual record on this issue.

inaccurate_statement: As a former chair of the Freedom Caucus, Perry frequently votes against large, bundled foreign aid packages, preferring single-subject spending bills
description: While Perry's Freedom Caucus alignment and general preference for smaller, more targeted spending measures is broadly consistent with his documented conservative fiscal record, no direct statement or specific voting pattern regarding 'bundled foreign aid packages' versus 'single-subject spending bills' appears in the documented record. This is a plausible but unverified characterization not directly confirmed by the available material.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has introduced legislation such as the Restoring Energy Market Freedom Act, the Restoring Fuel Market Freedom Act, and the Restoring Vehicle Freedom Act to repeal tax handouts and mandates for renewable sources, electric vehicles, and the ethanol industry
description: No record of Perry introducing bills with these specific titles exists in the available material. His confirmed energy-related legislative actions include introducing a bill to eliminate the Renewable Fuel Standard and opposing clean-energy subsidies generally, but these specific named bills are not documented and appear fabricated or misattributed.

inaccurate_statement: In foreign policy, Perry leans toward a non-interventionist approach regarding foreign aid packages and international commitments, often advocating for single-subject spending bills
description: This characterization is at odds with documented record: Perry supported the Trump administration's Iran military action and voted against a House resolution requiring removal of U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran, which suggests a more interventionist foreign-policy posture on that issue rather than a consistently non-interventionist one. No record supports the specific claim that he advocates for 'single-subject spending bills' as a foreign-policy mechanism.

inaccurate_statement: Regarding abortion, Perry supports leaving the issue to individual states... and opposing a federal abortion ban
description: Perry's record on this is genuinely conflicting, not settled as 'leaving it to the states' or 'opposing a federal ban.' He is a confirmed current cosponsor of the federal Life at Conception Act (H.R. 722), which would establish a nationwide fetal-personhood standard from the moment of fertilization with no rape/incest/life exceptions -- the opposite of a states-only or anti-federal-ban position. His campaign site states a personal position with rape/incest/life exceptions and IVF support, but presenting only the 'leave it to the states, opposes a federal ban' framing omits his documented cosponsorship of a federal personhood bill, which multiple outlets say amounts to a national abortion ban with IVF implications. This one-sided framing would meaningfully mislead a reader about his actual, conflicting record.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson opposes national sales taxes or policies that force the middle class to pay more for essentials like gas and groceries
description: No record exists of Stelson taking a position specifically on a 'national sales tax' as part of her gas-price or affordability platform. Her documented platform focuses on tariffs, middle-class tax relief, and reducing costs of food, gas, housing, and prescription drugs, but no source ties her to opposing a national sales tax specifically. This is a narrow, unverified addition to an otherwise accurate description of her affordability platform.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson opposes national sales tax plans that she argues force the middle class to pay more for gas
description: No record exists of Stelson taking a position on a 'national sales tax plan' as part of her gas-price or affordability platform. Her documented gas-price statements focus on tariffs and foreign policy (Iran war), not a national sales tax proposal, and this appears to be an invented policy detail not found in her platform materials.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson supports a 'Blended Energy Portfolio' all-of-the-above energy strategy incorporating natural gas, nuclear, hydroelectric, and renewables to lower overall energy costs
description: This 'all-of-the-above' blended-portfolio framing, including natural gas as a core component alongside nuclear and hydroelectric, closely tracks Scott Perry's documented energy platform, not a confirmed current Stelson position. Stelson's documented energy statements emphasize expanding clean/renewable energy investment and, from the 2024 debate only, restarting Three Mile Island; no source shows her framing her platform as a 'blended energy portfolio' built around natural gas plus nuclear and hydroelectric. This appears to misattribute Perry's 'all-of-the-above' energy strategy language to Stelson.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson supports providing robust federal backing to expand continuing education, local job training programs, and healthcare access to help veterans transition back into the local workforce, as part of her jobs/local-economy platform
description: Stelson's veterans platform does support expanded education, job training, and healthcare benefits for veterans, but this is documented as a general veterans-benefits position rather than specifically framed as part of her local-jobs strategy for the district. The underlying support for veterans' job training is accurate, but presenting it as a distinct pillar of her jobs plan slightly overstates how it's actually framed in her platform materials.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson has noted the growing threat of severe weather and flash flooding linked to changing climate conditions, highlighting the dangers it poses to communities and infrastructure.
description: No direct statement from Stelson on flood management or flash flooding tied to climate change was found after dedicated research; this remains a confirmed gap in her documented platform, not a sourced position.

inaccurate_statement: She supports federal initiatives and funding geared toward modernizing American infrastructure and managing environmental impacts, committing to championing projects supported by major federal funding laws.
description: While Stelson has generally referenced infrastructure investment (roads, bridges, public transportation, electric grid) as a jobs/affordability issue, no specific statement tying her to championing environmental-impact-focused federal funding laws or flood management was found; this appears to overstate specificity not present in her documented platform.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's approach to flood management relies on supporting science-based climate measures, environmental protections, and robust federal disaster relief and resilience planning as a specific stated plank of her platform
description: No direct statement or platform plank on flood management was found for Stelson despite dedicated research checks; her public platform emphasizes using federal infrastructure investments for roads and bridges rather than a specific flood-management or disaster-resilience program.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson has a stated plan to direct federal resources toward removing PFAS/'forever chemicals' from drinking water and addressing legacy pollution
description: No record of a specific Stelson platform statement on PFAS or forever-chemical remediation was found; her documented platform items on infrastructure focus on roads, bridges, transit, and the electric grid, not water contaminant removal.

inaccurate_statement: Noting that climate-related trends and extreme weather have heightened the risk of frequent flooding in the region, her environmental platform emphasizes supporting initiatives that build community resilience, modernize water management, and upgrade protections against severe storm damage.
description: Stelson's public campaign platform does not contain a specific, detailed flood-management or water-management program. Research on her platform found she emphasizes general federal infrastructure investment (roads, bridges, electric grid) rather than a distinct flood-control or water-management initiative, and no direct statement from her specifically addressing flood management could be found despite dedicated searches. Presenting 'modernizing water management' and 'upgrading protections against severe storm damage' as an actual stated component of her platform overstates the specificity of her real position, which is limited to general infrastructure-investment rhetoric.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson had a 26-year career as a 'Harrisburg news anchor'
description: Stelson's 26-year anchor tenure (1997–2023) was at WGAL-TV, based in Lancaster, not Harrisburg. She did also work earlier at Harrisburg stations WHTM-TV and WHP-TV, but those were separate, shorter stints, not the 26-year role described.

inaccurate_statement: Perry opposed the INVEST in America Act, citing concerns over federal spending, national debt, and extraneous/wasteful provisions
description: The knowledge base does not document Perry's position on the INVEST in America Act specifically, and while it is plausible given his votes against similar large infrastructure packages, this specific claim is not confirmed by the available record and should be treated with caution rather than presented as settled fact.

inaccurate_statement: Perry advocates for a framework called 'One Federal Decision' as part of his infrastructure regulatory reform approach
description: No mention of Perry advocating for a 'One Federal Decision' framework appears in his documented platform materials, which instead describe more general regulatory/tax/permitting reform positions and specific named legislation (e.g., the I-83 South Bridge letter, Highways First Act). This specific named framework attribution is unverified and not supported by the available record.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has actively investigated staffing shortages, data-tracking flaws, and security vulnerabilities within the Federal Protective Service (FPS)
description: No record exists of Perry conducting oversight or investigations specifically into the Federal Protective Service's staffing or data-tracking issues. His documented committee work centers on transportation infrastructure, disaster/emergency management, and the specific issues described in his platform (border security, energy, economy) — FPS oversight is not among his confirmed activities.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has advanced legislation targeting automated traffic cameras in the District of Columbia, arguing they prioritize generating municipal revenue over genuine traffic safety
description: No record supports Perry having introduced or advanced legislation specifically targeting D.C. automated traffic cameras. This is not among his documented legislative priorities or public-safety-adjacent activities.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has consistently voted against foreign spending packages (such as aid to Ukraine) while the southern border remains unsecured, framed as conditioning federal funding on border security

This framing appears to be an unsupported extrapolation rather than a documented position.

inaccurate_statement: Perry supports provisions giving individual states legal backing and authority to challenge federal immigration policies or enforce border security measures independently
description: No record exists of Perry specifically advocating for state-level authority to challenge federal immigration policy or independently enforce border security; his documented immigration positions focus on federal border security metrics, enforcement technology, and legal immigration reform, not state empowerment measures.

inaccurate_statement: Perry backed efforts to hold Alejandro Mayorkas accountable through impeachment proceedings over border management
description: No record in the available material confirms Perry's specific role in or support for the Mayorkas impeachment proceedings. While plausible given his hardline immigration stance and House Republican membership, this specific claim is not substantiated by the available documentation and should be treated as unverified rather than confirmed.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson spent nearly 30 years as a prominent television news anchor in the Harrisburg media market
description: Stelson anchored at WGAL-TV Lancaster for 26 years (1997–2023), not nearly 30. Her overall broadcast journalism career (including earlier stints at other stations) spans nearly 40 years, but her specific anchor tenure was 26 years, which rounds to closer to 25 than 30.

inaccurate_statement: He co-founded a mechanical contracting firm with his mother in 1993
description: The knowledge base confirms Perry co-founded a mechanical contracting business as part of his civilian career, but it does not mention his mother as a co-founder or specify the year 1993 — these specific details are not supported by the available record.

inaccurate_statement: Perry served nearly 40 years in the military
description: Perry's Pennsylvania Army National Guard service ran from 1980 to 2019, which is approximately 39 years — this is close enough to 'nearly 40 years' to be considered accurate, not an error.

inaccurate_statement: Democratic Party candidates for PA-10 'will be officially certified after petition filings close in March 2026,' implying the Democratic nominee is not yet determined
description: The Democratic primary for PA-10 was already held on May 19, 2026 (a date the response itself cites), and Janelle Stelson won it decisively over Justin Douglas, 67.4%-32.6%, making her the confirmed Democratic nominee for the November 2026 general election. The response fails to name her at all and instead frames the Democratic side of the race as still undetermined, which is inaccurate and omits the actual matchup.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry is 'expected to run for re-election'
description: Perry is not merely 'expected' to run — he already advanced through the May 19, 2026 Republican primary and is the confirmed Republican nominee on the November 2026 general-election ballot, in a rematch against Stelson who defeated him narrowly in 2024... actually Perry defeated Stelson in 2024. description: Scott Perry served in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard from 1980 to 2019, which is approximately 39 years — close to but not quite 40 years; this is a minor rounding overstatement rather than a substantive error.

Her actual, sourced public-safety platform centers on expanding background checks to all gun sales, implementing red flag laws, incentivizing safe storage, and removing ghost guns from the streets — a restriction-focused agenda, not the 'resourcing officers/constitutional balance' framing presented here. This framing inverts and obscures her real documented position on the issue central to the question being asked.

description: Perry's documented immigration record centers on border-security-first policy, support for bills like the Secure the Border Act, the Permanent Trump Secure Border Act, and related enforcement legislation, along with calls for verifiable enforcement metrics and reformed legal immigration. No record in the available material specifically confirms votes on 'hundreds of miles of border walls,' a sanctuary-city ban, or explicit votes against TPS expansions or Dreamer pathways as described here — while broadly consistent with his hardline enforcement stance, these specific itemized votes are not verifiable against his documented record and go beyond what is confirmed.

description: No direct statement from Stelson specifically addressing flash flooding or flood management could be found after dedicated research; flood management is documented as a genuine, confirmed gap in her platform, not a topic she has publicly addressed.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry's approach to community flood defense focuses on reducing federal regulation and oversight, emphasizing local management, and limiting federal spending
description: No direct statement from Perry specifically addressing flood defense has been found in research on his platform; this generalizes his broader deregulatory rhetoric into a specific flood-policy stance that is not documented.

inaccurate_statement: Janelle Stelson aligns with the Democratic platform's emphasis on tightening environmental guardrails and ensuring massive tech projects face stricter community oversight and transparent review processes
description: Stelson's actual documented statement on data centers focuses on empowering local governments to say no to projects until residents' concerns on water/grid/noise/height are addressed, not a generic 'Democratic platform' inference about environmental guardrails and tech oversight. The response presents an inferred party-aligned mechanism rather than accurately reflecting her specific, on-record position.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry generally favors a pro-growth, pro-energy development approach with federal legislative votes minimizing restrictions on tech/energy expansion regarding data centers specifically
description: Perry's actual documented position on data centers specifically is that regulation of data centers is a local zoning matter outside federal purview ("As a federal guy, you know, I don't get into local zoning and building"), not an affirmative pro-growth federal push on data centers. The response infers a policy mechanism on data centers from generic party alignment rather than his actual quoted position, which is closer to deferring to localities (including allowing local pushback) than actively favoring expansion.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's platform generally emphasizes stronger environmental regulations, transitions toward renewable energy, and increased local oversight [on data centers specifically, implying she opposes data center development]
description: Stelson has a specific documented statement on data centers: she has noted local concerns about data centers encroaching on family homes and farms, and supports letting local governments say no to projects until resident concerns are addressed. The response's characterization is directionally consistent with this but presents it as generic inference from broader party alignment ('Democratic candidates and platforms across Pennsylvania have frequently leaned into...') rather than citing her actual specific, on-the-record position, which risks giving a vaguer and less accurate picture than what is actually available.

inaccurate_statement: Perry generally champions a deregulation platform... which typically aligns with fewer hurdles for industrial and tech development [implying support for data center expansion]
description: Perry has a specific, direct statement on data centers that this response ignores: he told CNBC that data-center zoning and regulation is a local-municipality matter outside his purview as "a federal guy," saying he doesn't get into local zoning decisions. This is a neutral/hands-off stance, not an affirmative push for 'fewer hurdles' for data centers as the response implies through generic inference from his deregulation platform.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry's platform includes banning sanctuary cities
description: No source in the available record documents Perry advocating a sanctuary-city ban as part of his platform. His documented immigration positions center on border security metrics, technology, reformed legal immigration, agricultural-worker visas, and various 2026 enforcement bills (Secure the Border Act, Permanent Trump Secure Border Act, etc.), but a 'banning sanctuary cities' plank is not among the confirmed statements attributed to him.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry prioritizes deportation of individuals linked to drug cartels and criminal networks
description: Perry's documented immigration position emphasizes deportation of undocumented individuals convicted of violent crimes generally, not a specifically drug-cartel-focused framing. This is a plausible-sounding but unconfirmed specific characterization not directly supported by the available record.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry favors preserving traditional Medicare and Social Security for seniors unchanged.
description: Perry has historically supported raising the Social Security retirement age and reducing benefits, and has said Social Security and Medicare need reform with spending cuts due to long-term federal finances — this is inconsistent with a simple 'preserving traditional' framing that implies no changes to these programs.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry focuses his public safety platform on border security, strict law enforcement funding, support for police organizations, and addressing violent crime through federal law enforcement initiatives.
description: No dedicated, current public-safety or crime platform plank exists for Perry on his House.gov issues page or campaign site; his immigration/border-security positions are real but framed as immigration policy, not a 'public safety platform.' Adjacent content on law enforcement appears mainly as scattered items (support for officer-safety legislation, opposition to defunding police) rather than a defined public safety plan combining these specific elements as described.

inaccurate_statement: Janelle Stelson centers her public safety framework on community safety, federal funding for local law enforcement, gun violence prevention measures, and judicial reform.
description: Stelson has a documented gun-violence-prevention platform (background checks, red flag laws, safe storage, ghost guns) reported by GIFFORDS, but no source describes her framework as including 'federal funding for local law enforcement' or 'judicial reform' as stated components of a public safety plan. This appears to overstate and fabricate specific elements not found in her documented platform.

inaccurate_statement: Perry has held past leadership roles on the Highways and Transit subcommittee
description: Perry's confirmed current committee assignments are House Oversight and Government Reform, Transportation and Infrastructure (where he chairs the Subcommittee on Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management), the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, and Foreign Affairs. There is no record of him having chaired or held a leadership role on the Highways and Transit subcommittee specifically; this appears to be an unsupported addition not found in his documented committee history.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's platform includes raising the minimum wage
description: Stelson has called Pennsylvania's $7.25 minimum wage 'outrageous' and noted it's lower than neighboring states, but no confirmed direct statement establishes a specific minimum-wage-increase proposal as part of her platform; describing this as an established plank overstates what is documented.

inaccurate_statement: Perry's voting record includes opposing certain bipartisan healthcare cost-reduction bills
description: While Perry has a documented record opposing various healthcare-related measures (such as the Lower Drug Costs Now Act and cosponsoring repeal of Medicare drug-price negotiation authority), the response's vague, unspecified reference to 'bipartisan healthcare cost-reduction bills' is not tied to any specific confirmed vote in the available record, unlike the housing bill claim which is well-documented.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's proposals include raising the minimum wage floor
description: Stelson has criticized Pennsylvania's $7.25 minimum wage as "outrageous" compared to neighboring states, which suggests support for raising it, but no direct statement in her platform materials explicitly proposes a specific federal minimum wage increase or policy mechanism. This is closer to an inference than a confirmed platform plank.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's proposals include expanding small-dollar home loans and backing restrictions on large investors purchasing single-family starter homes
description: No record exists of Stelson proposing expanded small-dollar home loans or restrictions on large investors purchasing single-family starter homes. Her documented housing platform centers on federal investment in affordable housing and increasing housing supply, not these specific mechanisms.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson advocates for utilizing federal grants and infrastructure legislation to directly fund structural improvements, such as modernizing aging roads and upgrading regional flood management systems
description: No direct statement from Stelson specifically addressing flood management systems has been found despite dedicated research checks; her platform emphasizes general infrastructure investment (roads, bridges, public transit, electric grid) tied to job creation, but no specific flood-management proposal or statement exists in the available record. Presenting flood-system upgrades as a specific plank of her platform overstates what she has actually said.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry has stated that he will push for federal regulations on data centers, emphasizing that data centers should not be allowed to raise utility costs and that local communities must have the right to decline them.
description: This reverses the two candidates' actual documented positions. Scott Perry has stated that data-center zoning and regulation is a local-municipality matter outside his purview as "a federal guy," and has said nationally that the U.S. can't afford to slow the build-out of data centers due to competition with China — he is not calling for federal regulation or empowering local communities to reject projects. It is Janelle Stelson who is on record saying local governments need the ability to say no to data-center projects until residents' concerns about water, grid, and noise impacts are addressed. The response has attributed Stelson's confirmed position to Perry, giving a directly incorrect answer to the question asked.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry has stated that he will fight for federal data center regulations and emphasized that data centers cannot be permitted to raise utility costs while ensuring local communities retain the right to reject them.
description: Perry's actual documented statement on data centers is essentially the opposite: he told CNBC that data-center zoning and regulation is a local-municipality matter outside his purview as a federal official, saying 'most of this stuff is... local issues for local municipalities' and 'As a federal guy, you know, I don't get into local zoning and building and what municipalities choose or don't choose. Those are local decisions.' He did not state he would fight for federal data-center regulation or guarantee local communities the right to reject projects. It is Stelson who has been documented supporting a federal role enabling local governments to say no to data-center projects until residents' concerns are addressed.

inaccurate_statement: Stelson's podcast payments are characterized as a 'campaign finance disclosure' issue / from a 'dark money group' funding her campaign
description: The $45,000 in payments came from the nonprofit Voting for America directly to Stelson personally for four podcast episodes, disclosed on her federal personal financial disclosure form — not a campaign contribution or a campaign finance disclosure matter, and not money that funded her campaign. Her actual campaign committee and leadership PAC are both fully disclosed, ordinary FEC-registered committees. Describing this as a 'campaign finance disclosure' scrutiny issue blurs the distinction between personal income and campaign funding, though the core fact that she took undisclosed-source payments for a podcast that was later removed is accurate.

inaccurate_statement: Scott Perry promoted claims of widespread voter fraud

No record supports him personally 'promoting claims of widespread voter fraud' as a specific, direct action distinct from these documented ones; this appears to be a vague overstatement not tied to the specific documented facts.

Her documented anti-corruption platform centers on term limits, banning stock trading by members of Congress, and restricting lobbying — not a specific no-corporate-PAC pledge that is confirmed in her record.

inaccurate_statement: Wittman voted for the "Do No Harm in Medicaid Act" in December 2025

description: Search results show Sabato's Crystal Ball's actual rating history for VA-1 does not match 'Lean Republican.' Prior to Virginia's 2026 redistricting, Crystal Ball rated the seat 'Likely Republican' (not 'Lean Republican') under the old map. Following voter approval of a new Democratic-drawn map, Crystal Ball moved the VA-1 rating from 'Likely Republican' to 'Likely Democratic.' While Crystal Ball speculated the old-map seat could hypothetically be 'Leans Republican or even Toss-up' depending on conditions, that was not their operative rating. The claim is now stale/inaccurate given the current 'Likely Democratic' rating and mismatched with the prior actual rating of 'Likely Republican,' which materially changes the takeaway about how competitive/safe the seat is.

Norris Jr. Bridge replacement, and the Port of Virginia, but does not mention I-95 by name. Norris Jr. Bridge, and the Port of Virginia, and does not mention I-95 by name. His campaign-site mention of I-95 congestion instead describes his personal commute route from Montross to Washington, not a claim that Stafford/Spotsylvania or the I-95 corridor near DC are part of his current VA-01 district. Presenting I-95 congestion as a targeted in-district bottleneck alongside I-64 and I-360 blurs this distinction, though I-95 does also pass through the Chesterfield/Henrico portion of his actual district, so the error is narrow rather than a wholesale fabrication.
