This is a narrower factual inaccuracy that doesn't undermine the overall thrust of the response ragarding this incident.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke advocates for investing in high-speed broadband, roads, and bridges across rural communities as part of a formal infrastructure platform.
description: Cooke's official campaign platform has no dedicated 'Rural Infrastructure,' roads, or bridges plank. She has made a real, verified statement specifically about broadband access (comparing it to rural electrification), but the broader roads-and-bridges framing does not appear on her platform page and closely echoes language associated with a fake, look-alike campaign website rather than her actual campaign materials.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke calls for boosting investments in high-speed rural broadband, roads, and bridges as an infrastructure platform
description: Cooke's official campaign platform page has no formal 'roads and bridges' or infrastructure plank; the only independently verified statement on this topic is a single comment about treating broadband like rural electrification. A near-identical 'broadband, roads and bridges' phrasing traces to a typosquat/phishing site impersonating her campaign, not her real platform, so presenting a combined roads-and-bridges infrastructure commitment as her stated priority is unsupported overreach.

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden protects Medicaid and hospital funding in rural areas
description: Van Orden's record on Medicaid is genuinely mixed, not a clean 'protects' record. He voted for the 2025 reconciliation law that included Medicaid work-requirement tightening and a budget resolution setting up major Medicaid reductions, while separately voting in January 2026 (as one of 17 House Republicans nationally) to extend expiring ACA subsidies and securing some rural hospital/BadgerCare funding. Presenting this as simply 'protects Medicaid and hospital funding' omits the documented tension between his votes and characterizes a contested, two-sided record as a simple accomplishment.

inaccurate_statement: He completed five combat deployments, including tours in Bosnia, Afghanistan, and Iraq.
description: Van Orden's five combat deployments during his 26-year Navy SEAL career are confirmed, but no source in the available material specifies Bosnia, Afghanistan, and Iraq as the particular locations, so the specific countries named cannot be verified as accurate.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke has targeted Van Orden for prioritizing social media activity over congressional work, accusing him of taking credit for executive actions rather than delivering results through legislation
description: No record exists of Cooke making this specific 'social media over legislating' or 'taking credit for executive actions' attack line against Van Orden. This appears to be an invented characterization not found in the available material on her documented criticisms of him.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke criticized Van Orden for supporting failures to expand or extend ACA tax credit premium subsidies
description: Van Orden's actual record on this is more mixed than the response suggests: in January 2026 he was one of 17 House Republicans who crossed party lines to vote to extend expiring ACA subsidies, stating he would not let constituents lose coverage overnight. The response presents Van Orden as having simply failed to extend ACA subsidies, when his voting record includes a documented vote in favor of extending them (alongside other votes tightening Medicaid work requirements), a more nuanced record than depicted.

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden opposes federal environmental rules on agricultural waterways, arguing instead for voluntary farm stewardship, contending farmers use retention ponds and nutrient recycling rather than needing top-down federal intervention, specifically as a response to agricultural water contamination.
description: No direct statement from Van Orden on agricultural water contamination specifically was found in the available research; this remains a documented platform silence on that exact topic. He has expressed WOTUS-related regulatory concerns generally, but the specific 'voluntary stewardship via retention ponds and nutrient recycling' framing as his response to agricultural water contamination is not substantiated by any known source and appears to be an invented specific mechanism attributed to him without basis.

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden backed the multi-year Farm Bills, including 'the Farm, Food, and National Security Act,' which prioritize resource access and economic support over new environmental compliance restrictions.
description: No record exists of Van Orden's specific support for a bill by this name or of Farm Bill legislation being framed this way in relation to agricultural water contamination. This appears to be an unverified or possibly fabricated legislative title not found in his documented record.

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden is a member of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee
description: Van Orden's confirmed congressional committee assignments are Agriculture, Armed Services, and Veterans' Affairs (where he chairs the Economic Opportunity Subcommittee), plus co-chairing the Congressional Motorcycle Caucus. There is no record of him serving on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee.

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden utilizes his position on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee to direct federal Community Project Funding toward local road repairs, bridge maintenance, and community projects.
description: Van Orden's documented committee assignments are Agriculture, Armed Services, and Veterans' Affairs (where he chairs the Economic Opportunity Subcommittee), plus co-chairing the Congressional Motorcycle Caucus. There is no record of him serving on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee. While he has been involved in rural infrastructure funding events (e.g., a Sparta, WI road-improvement announcement with the U.S. Transportation Secretary), this appears unrelated to a Transportation and Infrastructure Committee seat, which is not documented as one of his assignments.

inaccurate_statement: He works on committees for Agriculture, Veterans' Affairs, and Transportation
description: His documented committee assignments are Agriculture, Armed Services, and Veterans' Affairs (Chairman, Economic Opportunity Subcommittee), plus Co-Chair of the Congressional Motorcycle Caucus — not Transportation. Armed Services is misidentified as Transportation.

inaccurate_statement: He completed five combat tours in places like Bosnia, Afghanistan, and Iraq
description: His five combat deployments as a Navy SEAL are confirmed, but no specific locations (Bosnia, Afghanistan, Iraq) are documented in the available record, making the specific place names an unverified addition to an otherwise accurate core fact.

inaccurate_statement: Act of Valor was a 2014 movie
description: Act of Valor, in which Van Orden appeared, was released in 2012, not 2014.

inaccurate_statement: Sits on House committees overseeing agriculture, veterans' affairs, and transportation
description: His documented committee assignments are Agriculture, Armed Services, and Veterans' Affairs (where he chairs the Economic Opportunity Subcommittee), not a transportation committee. No transportation committee assignment is documented.

inaccurate_statement: Often noted in public profile as the first enlisted Navy SEAL elected to Congress
description: Van Orden's public profile consistently touts him as the 'longest serving enlisted member of the United States military' ever elected to Congress, not the 'first enlisted Navy SEAL elected to Congress.' Search results confirm Van Orden and his campaign materials repeatedly use the 'longest serving enlisted member' framing (e.g., Wikipedia states his '26 years of active duty military service make him the longest serving enlisted member of the military in the history of Congress'). Moreover, the claim as stated is factually wrong: Scott Taylor, a former enlisted Navy SEAL, served as U.S. Representative for Virginia's 2nd district from 2017-2019, years before Van Orden's 2022 election, so Van Orden was not the first enlisted Navy SEAL elected to Congress. This is a narrower factual error/superlative mix-up rather than a claim that undermines the broader true point that Van Orden is a prominent Navy SEAL veteran in Congress, so severity is minor.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke will face Republican incumbent Derrick Van Orden on November 3, 2026
description: The 2026 U.S. general election is held on November 3? Actually the correct general election date for a November 2026 midterm is Tuesday, November 3, 2026 is incorrect — federal general elections are held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November, which in 2026 falls on November 3. Given no dossier contradiction on this specific date is found, this should not be flagged as inaccurate.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke holds a strong financial advantage with over $4.4 million in campaign funds
description: Reporting places Cooke's best-sourced fundraising total around $6.5 million as of a mid-2026 FEC filing (and later figures citing over $8 million), not $4.4 million. The $4.4 million figure appears to be a conflation with Van Orden's 2025 calendar-year fundraising total, which was reported as 'more than $4.3-4.4 million.' While Cooke has indeed outraised Van Orden overall by mid-2026, the specific $4.4 million figure attributed to her does not match documented reporting.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke will face Republican incumbent Derrick Van Orden on November 3, 2026
description: The 2026 U.S. general election is held on November 3? Actually the correct general election date for a November 2026 midterm is Tuesday, November 3, 2026 is incorrect — federal general elections are held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November, which in 2026 falls on November 3. Given no dossier contradiction on this specific date is found, this should not be flagged as inaccurate.

inaccurate_statement: Rebecca Cooke drew support from the DCCC as a moderate element of the party
description: Cooke received the DCCC's 'Red to Blue' designation, which is a standard national-party program supporting the party's chosen general-election nominee against a Republican incumbent — not specifically a marker of intra-party moderate support during the primary. Framing DCCC backing as evidence she drew support from the party's 'moderate elements' conflates general-election party support with primary-stage ideological alignment.

inaccurate_statement: Republican incumbent Derrick Van Orden ran unopposed in his primary
description: No evidence was found confirming whether Van Orden ran literally unopposed or simply received no coverage of a primary challenge; this is flagged in the available research as an open, unresolved question rather than a confirmed fact.

inaccurate_statement: Rebecca Cooke is in her second consecutive run for the seat
description: Rebecca Cooke has run for this seat three times total: she lost the 2022 Democratic primary to Brad Pfaff (never reaching the general election that year), lost the 2024 general election to Van Orden, and is now the 2026 nominee. This is her second consecutive general-election run against Van Orden, but her third run for the seat overall, so describing it simply as her 'second consecutive run for the seat' is imprecise and omits her 2022 primary run.

inaccurate_statement: Derrick Van Orden is seeking his third term in Washington, D.C.
description: Van Orden has served as U.S. Representative for WI-03 since January 3, 2023, after winning election in November 2022. If re-elected in November 2026, this would be the start of his third term (2023-2025 first term, 2025-2027 second term, 2027-2029 would be third), so 'seeking his third term' is actually accurate framing for the term he'd be starting; however, this is a borderline/ambiguous phrasing rather than a clear contradiction of the record, which shows two prior wins (2022, 2024) and now a third campaign.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke works across the aisle to secure federal funding for local police forces
description: No record exists of Cooke proposing or securing federal funding specifically for local police forces as a platform position; her documented statements on policing emphasize reallocating resources toward social workers, mental health services, and root-cause programs, alongside a general 'fully fund police' statement, not a specific funding-for-police-forces initiative or bipartisan legislative effort, since she has never held elected office.

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden advocates for tighter integration between federal agencies and local police to dismantle crime rings and secure communities
description: No source in the available material documents Van Orden making this specific 'federal/local partnerships to dismantle crime rings' proposal. His confirmed public safety platform centers on law enforcement funding/training and the HALT Fentanyl Act; this specific framing about federal-local integration to dismantle crime rings was not found and appears to be an embellishment beyond his documented positions.

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden's platform relies on free-market principles, deregulation, and spending cuts to address costs, rather than expanding government-backed insurance programs; Reducing Government Coverage: Van Orden has supported legislative measures aimed at cutting government healthcare spending
description: This omits that Van Orden was one of 17 House Republicans nationally who voted in January 2026 to extend ACA subsidies, stating he would 'not sit back and watch my constituents lose access to health care,' and separately claims to have secured $1 billion annually for BadgerCare and CMS approval preserving Wisconsin's hospital provider tax to protect Medicaid funding. Presenting his healthcare approach as simply 'reducing government coverage' and market-based deregulation, without any mention of these actions, is a one-sided characterization of a record that is genuinely mixed and conflicting.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke's national security framework focuses significantly on domestic resilience, protecting critical supply chains, and strengthening cybersecurity.
description: No statement or platform plank from Cooke specifically framing national security around supply-chain protection or cybersecurity was found. Her documented national-security-adjacent position is Pentagon oversight and opposition to new nuclear weapons types, which is different in substance from this characterization.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke favors a foreign policy rooted in strong international coalitions and diplomacy, viewing alliances like NATO as essential, and heavily supports international partnerships and democratic coalitions to counter adversaries.
description: No record of Cooke making statements about NATO, international alliances, or coalition-based foreign policy was found. This appears to be an inferred generic Democratic-alignment position rather than a sourced statement.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke's border-security approach 'focuses on comprehensive border management, technology, and legal pathways.'
description: Cooke's actual documented position calls for a 'secure border and a pathway to citizenship' via the bipartisan Dignity Act, and support for modern border technology and more immigration judges. The general thrust is roughly consistent, but 'comprehensive border management' is a vague characterization not directly sourced to her.

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden's approach is skeptical of open-ended foreign aid without strict benchmarks; tends to favor transactional foreign policy.
description: No record exists of Van Orden expressing skepticism toward foreign aid or describing a 'transactional' foreign policy approach. His documented positions emphasize strong military deterrence, support for Israel, and willingness to use force, with no specific statements found on foreign-aid conditionality.

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden actively supports a robust tariff strategy, arguing countries like Canada have long used unfair trade restrictions and dairy quotas to disadvantage American producers, and that standing firm with retaliatory measures forces trade partners to the table for fairer market access
description: No verified direct quote or statement from Van Orden specifically defending tariffs' effect on dairy farmers, or making this specific Canada/retaliatory-measures argument, was found. The dossier notes he has supported Trump's broader tariff policy and appeared with administration officials at dairy-related events, but this specific rationale and argument structure is not sourced to him.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke's platform advocates for ending trade wars, favoring expanded fair trade agreements and direct pipelines between local dairy cooperatives and international buyers
description: There is no record of Cooke proposing direct pipelines between local dairy cooperatives and international buyers or a specific 'fair trade agreements' expansion plank. Her documented tariff-related positions are general criticism of tariffs as harming farmers and workers, without this specific trade-pipeline mechanism.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke's broader rural strategy focuses on slowing farm consolidation and increasing credit access to keep family-owned dairies resilient
description: Cooke's documented platform includes opposing anti-competitive practices by large agricultural conglomerates and supporting small/midsize farms, but no specific 'credit access' program or an explicit 'slowing farm consolidation' framing was found. This appears to be an invented elaboration rather than a sourced position.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke served on the Wisconsin Economic Development Corporation [implying an elected or active governance role framing her manufacturing workforce platform]
description: Cooke's WEDC role was an appointed board position (January 2019–November 2021, appointed by Gov. Tony Evers), not an elected office, and she has never held elected office. The response does not explicitly call it elected, but citing it without that context risks implying more governmental authority than the appointed board-secretary/committee-co-chair role actually carried.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke campaigned with high-profile backing from the NRDC Action Fund
description: No NRDC Action Fund endorsement of Cooke is documented. Her documented endorsements include EMILY's List, Council for a Livable World, End Citizens United, labor unions, and various elected officials, but no NRDC Action Fund endorsement appears anywhere in the record. Per the endorsement guardrail, this is treated as a narrow, checkable, specific claim not resolved by the available material rather than a confirmed contradiction, but the complete absence of any environmental-endorsement mention combined with the specificity of naming this organization pushes it toward being flagged rather than silently accepted.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke pledges to champion cleaner water protections and general conservation funding aimed at broad ecological resilience across western Wisconsin
description: Cooke does have a genuine, documented water-quality platform plank (PFAS testing/remediation, addressing agricultural runoff/nitrates/algae blooms), but this is specifically targeted at PFAS and farm runoff, not framed as a broad 'ecological resilience' or general conservation funding initiative. The response's vague characterization overstates and generalizes a more specific, documented position.

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden voted in favor of the Water Resources Development Act (WRDA), which directly authorized funding for a flood risk investigation on the Mississippi, Black, and La Crosse Rivers
description: No record exists of Van Orden supporting a WRDA provision authorizing a flood risk investigation on the Mississippi, Black, and La Crosse Rivers. Flood protection is explicitly documented as a confirmed platform silence for Van Orden -- no direct statement or specific legislative record on flood protection was found in research, and this specific claim about a named WRDA provision and named rivers is not corroborated by any source.

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden co-introduced the bipartisan Dam Integrity Act, aiming to audit and upgrade aging structures within the USDA Watershed Program
description: No record exists of Van Orden co-introducing a 'Dam Integrity Act' or any dam-safety/USDA Watershed Program legislation. Flood protection and dam safety are not covered anywhere in his documented legislative record, which instead lists PFAS/water infrastructure funding, rural roads, and other specific accomplishments -- none involving dam safety or a bill by this name.

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden actively monitors local rail infrastructure during high-water events to enforce safety protocols and prevent toxic train washouts
description: No documentation exists of Van Orden engaging in rail-infrastructure monitoring during flood events or any train-washout safety initiative. This appears to be an invented claim with no basis in his documented record.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke focuses on public safety by targeting corporate and systemic crimes, focusing heavily on holding large corporations accountable for price gouging, corporate consolidation, and antitrust violations that financially harm families and rural hospitals
description: Cooke's antitrust and anti-price-gouging positions are real economic-policy planks, but no source frames these as part of her public-safety or crime-reduction approach. This response fuses her separate economic platform with her crime/public-safety positions into a synthesis not supported by any documented statement, similar to other confirmed misleading fusions of her distinct positions.

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden secured millions in federal Community Project Funding for regional public safety buildings, police equipment, and modern radio communications for first responders in western Wisconsin communities like West Salem and River Falls
description: Van Orden is documented as having sought federal funding for local public-safety infrastructure, including improved police/first-responder communications in River Falls, and secured an $8.4 million rural-infrastructure/road event in Sparta with the U.S. Transportation Secretary. However, no source ties him to a specific 'West Salem' public safety building project, and the specific combination of 'public safety buildings, police equipment, and modern radio communications' as a broad, multi-community accomplishment is not documented at this level of specificity. The general thrust that he has pursued public-safety infrastructure funding is accurate, but the added specificity (West Salem, police equipment, buildings) goes beyond what is confirmed.

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden has heavily championed and taken credit for a $50 billion federal rural healthcare infrastructure package, pointing to more than $200 million allocated to Wisconsin to maintain rural medical access
description: Van Orden's documented rural-health funding claims are a $1 billion/year BadgerCare figure and a $500 million rural-hospital infrastructure claim on his campaign site, plus a separately reported $204 million/year (over $1 billion over five years) Rural Health Transformation Fund figure and a Medicaid reimbursement rate increase from 1.8% to 6%. No source describes a '$50 billion federal rural healthcare infrastructure package' or a '$200 million allocated to Wisconsin' figure attributed to him; the actual national Rural Health Transformation Fund program (created by the 2025 reconciliation law) totals $50 billion nationally over several years, but the $200 million Wisconsin-specific figure does not match any documented number in his record ($204 million/year was the closest reported figure, not $200 million as a total, and not directly presented as something Van Orden personally 'took credit for' in this form).

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden recently highlighted state-level Medicaid provider assessment increases as a positive mechanism to bring billions in federal funding back to local institutions like Emplify Health by Gundersen
description: There is a documented claim that Van Orden secured CMS approval to grandfather Wisconsin's 6% hospital provider tax, preserving enhanced federal Medicaid funding for Wisconsin hospitals, but no record ties this specifically to 'Emplify Health by Gundersen' as a named institution or frames it in these exact terms.

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden highlights a $50 billion federal rural healthcare infrastructure package that designated over $200 million for facilities in Wisconsin
description: No record exists of a $50 billion federal rural healthcare infrastructure package with $200 million designated for Wisconsin facilities tied to Van Orden. His documented funding claims involve a $1 billion/year BadgerCare figure, a $500 million rural hospital infrastructure claim, and a $204 million/year, five-year Rural Health Transformation Fund allocation — none of which match this $50 billion/$200 million figure. This appears to be a fabricated or garbled statistic not grounded in any documented funding package.

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden has toured facilities like OakLeaf Clinics alongside administration officials to promote rural healthcare policies
description: Van Orden's documented rural healthcare facility tour with a federal official was at Marshfield Medical Center in Eau Claire with CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz in July 2026, not at a facility called OakLeaf Clinics. No record of an OakLeaf Clinics tour was found.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke supports protecting and expanding rural healthcare access, focusing on securing long-term operational funding rather than one-time infrastructure grants.
description: Cooke's platform does include general pledges to increase Medicare/Medicaid reimbursement rates for rural hospitals, but no source frames this explicitly as 'long-term operational funding rather than one-time infrastructure grants' in contrast to Van Orden's approach; this framing appears to be an unsupported editorial construction rather than a documented position.

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden has advocated for a $50 billion rural healthcare infrastructure bill, highlighting that it allocated over $200 million to Wisconsin to improve rural medical access.
description: No record exists of Van Orden advocating for a '$50 billion rural healthcare infrastructure bill' with '$200 million to Wisconsin.' His confirmed rural-health funding claims are different figures: a claimed $1 billion annually for BadgerCare, $500 million for rural hospital infrastructure, and a separate $204 million annually through the Rural Health Transformation Fund. The specific $50 billion bill and $200 million Wisconsin allocation described here do not match any documented figure and appear to be fabricated or badly conflated.

inaccurate_statement: He has toured facilities like the OakLeaf Clinics in Eau Claire alongside federal health officials to push for regulatory improvements tailored to rural clinics.
description: No record exists of Van Orden touring 'OakLeaf Clinics' in Eau Claire. His documented healthcare-facility visit was to Marshfield Medical Center in Eau Claire with CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz in July 2026, not OakLeaf Clinics. This appears to be a fabricated or misattributed detail.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke's platform highlights and aligns with community activists who successfully stalled a proposed $1.6 billion hyperscale data center in Menomonie
description: No source in the available research material documents a specific $1.6 billion Menomonie data center project being stalled by activists Cooke aligned with, or any such named local intervention. This specific dollar figure and project location was not found and appears fabricated or unverifiable.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke's platform in the primary era favored federal support for local municipal transparency to give communities tools to fight secretive developments
description: This describes her earlier primary-era framing accurately as far as the transparency emphasis goes, but the response omits that her position appears to have shifted to an explicit federal moratorium by the general election, presenting only the softer framing as her current stance without noting the apparent shift.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke explicitly supports the American Dream and Promise Act
description: Cooke's documented support for DACA-related protections for immigrants brought to the U.S. as children is confirmed, but no record ties her specifically to the American Dream and Promise Act by name; her documented direct statement on border/immigration policy references the Dignity Act, not this specific bill.

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden frequently points to a heavily publicized assault case in Prairie du Chien involving unauthorized immigrants to argue for stricter border controls
description: No record exists of Van Orden citing a specific Prairie du Chien assault case involving an unauthorized immigrant as part of his immigration messaging. Prairie du Chien appears in his background only in connection with a 2021 library confrontation over a Pride Month display, an unrelated matter. This specific claim about a named local criminal case is not supported by any documented statement or reporting.

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden's campaign ties his opponent to progressive policing and immigration policies, claiming her approach is too weak to ensure community safety
description: There is no documented instance of Van Orden or his campaign making this specific characterization of Cooke's immigration/policing stance as a defined campaign attack line, though attacks referencing her 'defund the police' comments are documented in a different context (2023-2024 remarks, not immigration-specific).

inaccurate_statement: Cooke agrees that the southern border must be fully secured to address local drug trafficking and safety concerns.
description: Cooke's actual stated immigration position emphasizes a 'commonsense immigration policy that includes a secure border and a pathway to citizenship' and support for the bipartisan Dignity Act, with no mention of drug trafficking or fentanyl. The drug-trafficking/cartel framing in reporting comparing the two candidates is specifically attributed to Van Orden, not Cooke, so attributing this framing to Cooke misattributes rhetoric more characteristic of her opponent.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke campaigns on repairing roads 'from the driveway to the highway' with good-paying union jobs, tied to a source labeled 'Instagram·repdrake'
description: No record exists of Cooke making a specific roads/highway union-jobs statement, and her official campaign platform page contains no formal roads or bridges plank. Her only confirmed related statement is about broadband ('treat broadband like rural electrification'), not roads or highways specifically. The cited source name also does not correspond to any known outlet or the candidate's own campaign material.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke backs robust federal investments aimed at modernizing rural transit networks, roads, and bridges.
description: Cooke's official campaign platform page contains no 'Rural Infrastructure,' roads, or bridges plank. Her only verified statement in this space is a comment specifically about broadband access, not roads, bridges, or transit networks; a formal platform commitment on roads/bridges has not been confirmed.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke argues that smaller municipalities and rural areas have been overlooked in infrastructure allotments and pledges to target funds specifically for local roadways.
description: No source confirms Cooke has made a specific pledge about targeting funds for local roadways; her campaign platform page does not include a roads/bridges plank, and her only documented infrastructure-adjacent comment concerns broadband access, not roadways.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke's transport platform is backed by a prominent endorsement from former U.S. Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg.
description: Pete Buttigieg has endorsed Cooke and campaigned for her, but there is no documented basis for characterizing this as an endorsement specifically of a Cooke 'transport platform' — the endorsement is a general campaign endorsement, not tied to a specific infrastructure or transportation policy platform.

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden is a member of the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.
description: Van Orden's documented committee assignments are Agriculture, Armed Services, and Veterans' Affairs (where he chairs the Economic Opportunity Subcommittee), plus co-chairing the Congressional Motorcycle Caucus. There is no record of him serving on the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke centers her platform on investing heavily in rural infrastructure, framing it as an essential tool to boost the economy and create union jobs, and advocates ensuring federal tax dollars flow into fixing local roads
description: Cooke's official campaign platform page has no dedicated 'Rural Infrastructure,' roads, or bridges plank, and no formal platform commitment on roads/highways is confirmed. Her only verified statement in this space is a single comment about treating broadband like rural electrification — not a broader roads/highways investment plan with union-jobs framing. Presenting road/highway investment as a central plank of her platform overstates what is actually confirmed.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke rejects the 'defund the police' platform, maintaining a moderate approach.
description: Cooke's record is more nuanced than a clean rejection: in 2023-2024 she made comments favoring reallocating some police funding toward 'root causes' and social workers, which were widely characterized as defund-adjacent. When asked directly, she said she supports fully funding police departments while adding social services — not a simple rejection of the defund framing as the response implies.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke's platform treats poverty and housing affordability, alongside the opioid crisis, as foundational drivers of local crime, tying her affordable-housing plank directly to her crime-reduction rationale.
description: Cooke's documented 'root causes' approach to crime centers on reallocating some police funding toward social workers, mental health services, and de-escalation training — not housing affordability. She separately has an affordable-housing plank, but it appears under her general economic priorities, not as part of a stated crime-reduction rationale. No source ties her housing policy directly to crime reduction, so presenting it as part of her crime platform fuses two real but distinct positions into an unsupported synthesis.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke is a member of the Wisconsin Economic Development Corporation
description: Cooke served on the Wisconsin Economic Development Corporation board as an appointed member from January 2019 to November 2021, a term that has ended; describing her as currently 'a member' without noting this was a past, appointed (not elected) role from 2019-2021 is imprecise, though the underlying fact of her having served is accurate.

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden champions initiatives that tie employment benefits, matching retirement funds, and domestic financial protection to keeping wealth within local communities
description: No evidence supports this claim. Web searches for Van Orden's legislative record and issue positions turn up his actual priorities—VA home loan reform, Social Security Fairness Act, agriculture, veterans' benefits—but nothing resembling an initiative tying 'employment benefits, matching retirement funds, and domestic financial protection to keeping wealth within local communities.' This phrase is vague, jargon-like, and does not match any bill, press release, or issue page attributable to Van Orden. It appears to be fabricated or invented language with no basis in his actual record.

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden highlights securing over $200 million in 2026 for Wisconsin via the Rural Health Transformation Program
description: The documented figure for Wisconsin's Rural Health Transformation Fund allocation is $204 million annually for five years, totaling over $1 billion, not a one-time $200 million figure as implied. The claim is directionally close but imprecisely characterizes the funding structure.

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden introduced bipartisan legislation to increase veterans' access to non-opioid pain medications
description: No record exists of Van Orden introducing legislation specifically on veterans' access to non-opioid pain medications. His confirmed veterans-related legislative work includes the VA Home Loan Affordability Act and general VA accountability and benefits advocacy, but this specific non-opioid pain medication bill is not documented.

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden advocates for repealing the ACA
description: Van Orden's campaign site does use repeal-and-replace framing, but his actual voting record is more mixed: in January 2026 he was one of 17 House Republicans nationally who voted with Democrats to extend expiring ACA subsidies, saying he would not watch constituents lose coverage overnight. His communications director clarified this was not an endorsement of the underlying law. Presenting a flat 'advocates for repealing the ACA' framing omits this documented cross-party vote and the genuine tension between his campaign rhetoric and his actual legislative action.

inaccurate_statement: Van Orden's rural hospital support was achieved by 'leveraging state-level provider tax changes'
description: The confirmed action was federal, not state-level: in July 2026 Van Orden secured CMS (federal) approval to grandfather Wisconsin's 6% hospital provider tax, preserving enhanced federal Medicaid funding for Wisconsin hospitals. Describing this as a 'state-level' change mischaracterizes the nature of the action, though the underlying substance (provider-tax related support for rural hospitals) is real.

inaccurate_statement: Rebecca Cooke focuses on aggressive investment in new roads, bridges, and regional transportation as part of her platform
description: Cooke's campaign platform page has no 'Rural Infrastructure,' roads, or bridges plank. The only verified statement she has made in this space is a single comment about treating broadband like rural electrification — there is no confirmed formal roads/bridges platform commitment, so characterizing this as a central, 'aggressive' roads-and-bridges investment plank overstates what is actually on record.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke links road upgrades specifically to helping family farmers and small businesses lower transit costs and move goods smoothly out of rural areas
description: No statement from Cooke tying road-specific infrastructure investment to farm/small-business transit costs has been found; her confirmed infrastructure-adjacent comment is limited to broadband access, not roads.

inaccurate_statement: Cooke's platform includes widening rural road shoulders so large-scale farming equipment can pass safely
description: No confirmed platform plank or statement from Cooke specifically proposes widening road shoulders for farm equipment.
